The database must be deployable across various physical nodes and cloud regions, offering flexibility in scaling operations. The solution must also include non-intrusive, near real-time Change Data Capture (CDC) capabilities, enabling seamless data updates to the SDP. The solution must support multi-cloud hybrid deployments, allowing integration across Data Centers, On-Premise, VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC), GovCloud, and Microsoft Azure Government (MAG) environments. Geo-partitioning is required to optimize latency and ensure consistent and responsive performance for VA operations nationwide. The solution must also provide resilience and elastic scaling to handle machines, datacenter, and regional failures, maintaining continuous operation without manual intervention. Together, these capabilities enable VA to accurately capture operational data and deliver near real-time insight and analytics, ensuring decision makers and customer service staff have accurate, current information to better serve Veterans. The Contractor shall provide up to 300 hours of incidental services support within the 12-month licensing period. title: Sweden – Financial analysis software package – ALM System and Services
description: The Swedish National Debt Office (Riksgälden), hereinafter referred to as “SNDO”, requires an Asset and Liability Management (ALM) system and related services, including software licences or subscriptions, implementation, operation, maintenance, support, training and consultancy services, hereinafter collectively referred to as the “ALM System and Services”. The ALM System will be used to perform asset and liability management analyses relating to the system for financing nuclear decommissioning and waste management in Sweden, hereinafter referred to as the “Financing System”. The primary purposes of the analyses are to: a) assess the risk that the assets and future income of the Financing System will be insufficient to meet its future liabilities, including the calculation and analysis of the Risk Margin; and b) support decisions concerning the strategic asset allocation of the Nuclear Waste Fund. The Agreement will enter into force when it has been signed by both parties, which is expected to occur in December 2026. Implementation, model configuration, testing and other activities required for production deployment shall commence following the entry into force of the Agreement. The ALM System shall be approved and ready for production use no later than 1 January 2027. The operational services period will commence on 1 January 2027. The initial operational services period will be three (3) years. Thereafter, the Agreement will be automatically extended for successive periods of one (1) year at a time, unless terminated by SNDO in accordance with the Agreement. The maximum operational services period, including all extensions, is eight (8) years. The procurement is not divided into separate lots. For organisational, functional and risk-related reasons, SNDO requires the ALM System and Services to be provided as a single, integrated delivery. The assignment requires the Supplier to assume overall responsibility for the implementation, functionality, operation, support and maintenance of the ALM System and for the coordination of the related services throughout the contract period. Dividing the procurement into separate lots would make it more difficult to ensure coherent functionality, clear allocation of responsibility and effective implementation and operation. SNDO therefore considers that dividing the procurement into separate lots would not be appropriate.

title: Norway – Network equipment – Dynamic purchasing system for supplementary procurements, assistance and consultancy services for network systems and equipment.
description: Background The contracting authority needs to establish a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) for supplementary procurements, assistance and consultancy of network systems and equipment. The need is for the replacement of older equipment and continual procurements for the existing network platform. The network infrastructure supports mission critical functions. Therefore it is necessary to ensure stable access to compatible equipment over time, as well as facilitate high security of delivery, quick handling at errors and robust supply chains. A DPS gives the contracting authority flexibility for varying purchasing needs and at the same time an option for an efficient competition for the individual procurements within the scheme. The scheme shall contribute to the continuation of a standardised network platform with systems that can be integrated easily, administered efficiently and support centralised operation, monitoring and logging. Description of the delivery The scheme includes the establishment of a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) for supplementary procurements, assistance and advice for network systems and equipment with the accompanying licences, software subscriptions, support and manufacturer guarantee. The DPS shall cover the contracting authority ́s ongoing need for compatible equipment for the existing network platform. Procurements under the dynamic purchasing system will include equipment within the following categories: Computer centre equipment for SDN core Gateway, routers and aggregation Branch routes, distribution and access switches WiFi Firewall and Security Components Assistance and advice. The delivery can also include spare parts, simple replacement services in the event of errors, documentation, marking, assembly in rack and physical installation. Broad product coverage and high compatibility with the current network platform are requested, so that management, configuration and operation can be carried out equally across the environments as far as possible. Call-offs may require compatibility with the contracting authority ́s technical platform, as stated in Annex 1 - Technical Platform. The scheme shall allow for predictable access to relevant and compatible models, a quick response with errors or capacity needs, as well as supporting safe and stable operation of the contracting authority ́s network infrastructure.

title: Finland – Software package and information systems – Crypto Asset Tax Calculation Solution
description: Crypto Asset Tax Calculation Solution The Finnish Tax Administration seeks to procure a production-ready software solution for the processing, analysis and tax calculation of crypto-asset transaction data. The purpose of the procurement is to support tax assessment, tax control, tax audits and analytical activities related to crypto-assets. The solution will be used to analyse cryptocurrency transaction histories, determine the tax consequences of crypto-asset transactions and produce information that can be further utilised within the Finnish Tax Administration’s internal processes and systems. The procurement concerns a software solution capable of importing, processing, analysing and exporting cryptocurrency transaction data originating from multiple sources. Such data may be obtained from taxpayers, cryptocurrency exchanges and trading platforms, cryptocurrency wallet applications, blockchain addresses and other sources of cryptocurrency transaction information. The solution is intended to support the Finnish Tax Administration in the examination of cryptocurrency transaction histories, identification and classification of transactions, reconstruction of transaction chains, identification of transfers between wallets and service providers, calculation of capital gains and capital losses, and application of cryptocurrency tax rules. In addition, the solution shall support the export of transaction and calculation data for further processing within the Finnish Tax Administration. The solution may be used both as a standalone tool for cryptocurrency transaction analysis and tax calculations and as a source of transaction and calculation data for use within the Finnish Tax Administration’s internal systems. The primary objectives of the procurement are to improve the efficiency of processing cryptocurrency transaction histories, increase the transparency and traceability of tax calculations, enable independent verification of calculation results, ensure the availability of transaction and calculation data in reusable formats and reduce the amount of manual work required in the analysis and taxation of cryptocurrency transactions. The procurement includes software licences, access to the production environment, user documentation, training materials, technical support services and the related rights and deliverables specified in the procurement documents. Detailed functional, technical, operational and licensing requirements are set out in the appendices to the Call for tenders.

title: Ireland – E-learning services – TR5866 A Single Supplier Framework Agreement Digital Learning Design, Development and Maintenance Services pursuant to a framework agreement
description: The Contracting Entity intends to procure a Digital Learning Design, Development and Maintenance Services framework for the provision of specialist digital learning services, including instructional design, eLearning development, accessibility reviews, project management and associated support services. The successful tenderer will be required to work collaboratively with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and stakeholders to design, develop, review, test and deliver digital learning content from initial onboarding through to final approval and provision of SCORM-compliant outputs. The supplier will be expected to provide a structured and transparent development methodology, supported by appropriate governance, project management, universal design principles including accessibility, quality assurance and stakeholder engagement processes. It is proposed that the Framework will include (non-exhaustive list – high level scope): Create engaging, accessible and effective digital learning that keeps learner needs, content and learning objectives central to the design. Examples of digital learning topics and types include: Policy, process or compliance learning Systems, technical or operational training Bite-sized learning, such as microlearning, video or animation Develop digital learning materials using the ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation and Evaluation) framework, ensuring learning objectives, activities and assessments align with Bloom’s Taxonomy and the needs of the target audience. Use purposeful interactive approaches to enhance learner engagement. Apply Universal Design for Learning (UDL) and accessibility by design principles throughout, ensuring compliance with WCAG 2.2, EN 301 549 and ESB accessibility requirements, and meeting accessibility best practices. Ensure all interactive elements are accessible, usable and support diverse learner needs, undertaking additional development where required to meet accessibility requirements. Undertake accessibility testing as part of the design, development and quality assurance process, using appropriate testing methods and tools, and remediate identified accessibility issues prior to final delivery and approval. Provide appropriate coaching, guidance and instructional design support to SMEs within the business. Project manage the end-to-end development of digital learning solutions, from the business’s SME onboarding to final delivery, including appropriate project planning, timelines, milestones, review stages, change management and stakeholder approval/sign-off. Provide user friendly collaboration tools that enable SMEs to review content, give feedback, track changes and monitor progress. Apply internal governance and quality assurance controls to ensure all deliverables meet ESB’s scope, requirements, timelines and quality standards. Provide access to a library of pre-existing digital learning modules on standard or commonly required topics (e.g. data protection, cybersecurity, health and safety, compliance or similar). Where appropriate, these modules should be capable of reasonable customisation to incorporate ESB branding, accessibility requirements and organisation-specific information. Digital learning content must be developed using a recognised, globally adopted authoring tool (e.g. Articulate 360 or equivalent). Provide all content in a SCORM-compliant format. Ensure compatibility with ESB’s current Learning Management System (SuccessFactors) on desktop, mobile and tablet devices. Provide access to a dedicated team with the skills and capacity required to deliver services to ESB, including an ESB Account Lead, Instructional Designers, eLearning Developers, QA/Accessibility Specialists, Project Managers and additional creative team e.g. Graphic Designers/ Illustrators and Animators.

title: FY27 NIH OFM 1099Pro
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTATIONS OR PROPOSALS This Notice of Intent is issued solely for informational purposes. The Government intends to award a sole source contract and is not seeking competitive quotations or proposals. No solicitation document exists for this requirement, and a Request for Quotation (RFQ) will not be issued. Intended Contractor SOVOS Compliance LLC 1055 Howell Mill Road NW, Suite 750 Atlanta, GA 30318-5557 Description of Requirement The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of Financial Management (OFM), requires the continued use of the SOVOS 1099 Pro tax reporting solution and associated Service Bureau services. The requirement includes the following software licenses: 1099 Pro Enterprise Desktop 1099 Pro 1042-S Pro W-2 Pro These licenses and associated services support NIH's annual federal tax information reporting responsibilities for payments made to vendors, contractors, foreign recipients, employees, and other reportable payees. The software must provide OFM with the capability to: Import and manage tax reporting data; Validate taxpayer and payment information; Prepare Forms 1099, 1042-S, and W-2; Process corrections and amended filings; Reconcile reportable amounts; Generate records in formats required for federal tax reporting; Electronically file returns with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) through the Information Returns Intake System (IRIS); Reprint recipient tax forms as necessary; and Support submission of corrected or replacement filings. The software must be deployable on NIH premises and support the printing of approximately 20,000 tax forms annually. The contractor shall ensure that all filing and mailing activities are completed in accordance with applicable IRS and Social Security Administration (SSA) deadlines and requirements. The software solution must maintain a FedRAMP Authorized designation at a level appropriate to the Government's requirements. Period of Performance The anticipated period of performance consists of one (1) 12-month base period: December 17, 2026, through December 16, 2027 Sole Source Rationale SOVOS Compliance LLC is the only known source capable of providing a FedRAMP-authorized version of the 1099 Pro tax reporting solution together with the integrated Service Bureau services currently utilized by NIH OFM. The SOVOS Service Bureau is an integral component of NIH OFM's tax reporting process because it provides the production and filing services necessary to complete the reporting lifecycle after OFM reviews and approves tax data. These services include: Printing and mailing recipient tax statements; Electronically filing applicable information returns with the IRS and SSA; and Supporting corrected and replacement filings, as required. Together, the 1099 Pro software licenses and Service Bureau services provide NIH OFM with an established end-to-end capability for preparing, validating, furnishing, correcting, and filing required tax information returns within statutory and regulatory deadlines. The SOVOS solution enables timely and accurate processing of large volumes of tax reporting data while maintaining continuity with existing NIH business processes and systems. Annual software updates are required to ensure compliance with changes to IRS and SSA forms, filing specifications, validation requirements, reporting thresholds, and electronic filing standards. These licenses and services must be renewed annually, and SOVOS releases updated versions each year to maintain compliance with current federal tax reporting requirements. Responses to this Notice This notice is not a request for competitive proposals, quotations, or bids. However, interested parties may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to meet the Government's requirements as described herein. Responses received will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether a competitive procurement should be conducted in the future. The determination not to compete this proposed contract action is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred by respondents in connection with this notice. Questions Questions or comments regarding this Notice of Intent shall be submitted via email only to: Em'Ria J. Briscoe Contract Specialist Email: emria.briscoe@hhs.gov Please include the following subject line: Notice of Intent Question Submission � FY27 NIH OFM 1099 Pro Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. INTRODUCTION The Aircraft Project Management Office (AIR PMO), under the Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager Robotic Autonomous Systems (DRPM RAS), is conducting market research regarding commercially available and emerging Group 1 and Group 2 Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Training, Mission Planning, Mission Rehearsal, Simulation, and Qualification Management Systems. For market research and planning purposes, the Government is seeking information regarding industry�s ability to provide and support these capabilities at scale. Potential future demand could involve thousands of training devices, simulator stations, software licenses, or equivalent deployed units. However, no procurement quantity, acquisition strategy, or requirement has been established, and any quantities referenced in this RFI are illustrative planning assumptions only. The Government requests white papers from interested parties with commercially available or emerging capabilities. Responses will assist the Government in identifying potential solutions; understanding technical approaches, system maturity, interoperability, scalability, implementation considerations, and business models; refining capability objectives and potential requirements; and informing acquisition planning and potential procurement strategies. This RFI follows the Air PMO virtual Industry Day conducted on 03 September 2026. Participation in the Industry Day is not a prerequisite for responding to this RFI. This RFI is an independent Air PMO market research effort and is not associated with or conducted in support of the Drone Dominance Program. BACKGROUND Simulation-based training has the potential to enhance operator proficiency, improve training availability, increase training throughput, reduce operational risk, and provide realistic Mission Planning and Mission Rehearsal capabilities for Group 1 and Group 2 UAS. Simulation-based training may also reduce operational impacts associated with range availability, airspace restrictions, spectrum congestion, weather delays, aircraft maintenance requirements, and logistical constraints while supporting standardized, repeatable, and scalable training across multiple UAS platforms. The Government seeks to understand current industry capabilities, technology maturity, innovative approaches, best practices, and limitations relevant to these objectives. title: Acadia National Park
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for Acadia National Park, Project ME NP ACAD BRG(2), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000002, located in Hancock County, Maine. The project consists of repair of Main Route 233, Paradise Hill, and Frazer Creek Bridges. The work includes reconstruction of asphalt concrete pavement and aggregate base course, placement of structural backfill, cleaning and removing debris from weepholes and inlets, cleaning and sealing joints, erosion repair, repointing mortar joints, placing waterproofing membrane to improve the service life, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $2,000,000 to $3,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about October 9, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will not be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. description: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) is to issue this Request for Proposal (RFP) HM047626R0018 for public response for the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) Human Resource Management II (HRM II). The HRM II RFP will be a commercial effort under FAR Part 12, and the Government anticipates using Best Value � Tradeoff evaluation methods and acquisition procedures as described in FAR Part 15. Contract award will be made to the offeror who provides the best overall value to the Government in terms of evaluation factors listed in Section 5 of the RFP. The procurement will be conducted using full and open competition procedures. The Government contemplates award of a performance-based contract using Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and Time-and-Materials (T&M) CLINs resulting from the solicitation. The period performance is anticipated to be a one (1) year base period with four (4) twelve (12) month option periods. The HRM II acquisition includes: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency requires comprehensive Human Resource Management support services across the employee lifecycle. The requirement includes support for functions such as personnel data processing, talent acquisition support, talent development support, strategic workforce planning, employee support services, performance records management, benefits processing, retirement tracking, and related HR management support activities. In order to be considered for this requirement, the offeror shall have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), https://www.sam.gov. Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://www.sam.gov. Registration MUST contain the appropriate North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 541612 � Human Resources Consulting Services Size Standard $29M. ***Amendment 0003 � Solicitation Update*** The Government is issuing Amendment 0003 to Solicitation No. HM047626R0018 for HRM II. The purpose of this amendment is to revise solicitation instructions and extend key solicitation dates. Summary of Changes: 1. This amendment incorporates Attachment 16, Supplemental Section 4 � Instructions, Conditions, and Notices to Offerors, Revision 3, and updates the following sections: - Section 4.4(A) � General Proposal Instructions - Section 4.5 � Information to Offerors - Section 4.7(F) � Solicitation Question and Answer Period - Section 4.7(G) � Proposal Submission and Due Date - Section 4.10(C) � Volume 2 � Factor 1: Technical/Management Approach Subfactors 2. title: Belgium – Educational software development services – ONTWIKKELING VAN E-LEARNINGPROGRAMMA’S EN -MODULES OVER OVERHEIDSOPDRACHTEN EN DE FINANCIËLE ORGANISATIE VAN DE BRUSSELSE GEMEENTEBESTUREN EN OCMW’S
description: Objets des services du marché : DEVELOPPEMENT DE PROGRAMMES ET DE MODULES DE FORMATION EN E-LEARNING DANS LES THEMATIQUES DES MARCHES PUBLICS ET DE L’ORGANISATION FINANCIERE DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. Le marché public est divisé en lots. Les soumissionnaires sont libres d’introduire une offre pour un ou pour plusieurs lots. L’ensemble des lots organisés par le présent marché visent à l’élaboration, la conception technique, la médiatisation, le développement, la livraison, l’intégration avec support technique dans la plateforme LMS de l’ERAP ainsi que la maintenance de trois modules de formation/apprentissage au format e-learning, disponibles simultanément en versions française et néerlandaise. Les lots 1, 2 et 3 visent l’élaboration de trois programmes d’apprentissage (objectifs, contenus, dispositif pédagogique) rendus disponibles en langue française et destinés à s’intégrer dans des modules en e-learning. Ces 3 programmes portent sur les trois thématiques suivantes : - « Introduction aux achats publics des administrations communales et des CPAS bruxellois ». - « Introduction à l’organisation financière des administrations communales bruxelloises ». - « Introduction à l’organisation financière des CPAS bruxellois ». Les lots 4 et 5 visent la conception technique, la médiatisation, le développement technique et la maintenance des trois modules de formation au format e-learning sur base des trois programmes d’apprentissage susmentionnés. Hébergement des modules e-learning : les modules de formation e-learning seront hébergés sur la plateforme LMS de l’ERAP (voir description technique en annexe). Le cas échéant, les modules e-learning seront hébergés sur la plateforme LMS d’un ou plusieurs administrations clientes ou sur un site Internet. Il est à noter que le présent marché ne couvre pas les services liés à l’intégration des modules e-learning sur d’autres plateformes que celle mise à disposition par l’ERAP. Durée des modules e-learning : Les modules de formation au format e-learning visés par les lots 4 et 5 ont une durée respective estimée à 60 minutes (2 x 30 min. ou 4 x 15 min.). Thématique des modules : Ces modules s’intègrent dans un parcours de formation plus large destiné à l’onboarding des agents de niveau A, B ou C des administrations communales et des CPAS de la Région de Bruxelles-capitale. Estimation du nombre d’utilisateurs finaux pour chacun des trois modules d’apprentissage : environ 550 personnes par an (500 apprenants/utilisateurs finaux et 50 responsables représentants les administrations concernées + personnel ERAP). Durée du marché : pour tous les lots, le marché est conclu pour une durée d’un an, renouvelable trois fois pour la même durée, pour une durée totale de 4 ans (voir point II.7 pour les détails). Le marché est divisé en lots de la manière suivante : (1) LOT 1 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION AUX ACHATS PUBLICS DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (2) LOT 2 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES BRUXELLOISES. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (3) LOT 3 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (4) LOT 4 : CONCEPTION, MÉDIATISATION, DÉVELOPPEMENT, LIVRAISON, INTEGRATION DANS LA PLATEFORME LMS ERAP AVEC SUPPORT TECHNIQUE ET MAINTENANCE DU MODULE E-LEARNING D’INTRODUCTION AUX ACHATS PUBLICS DES COMMUNES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS (DURÉE ESTIMÉE : 60 MINUTES), EN VERSIONS FRANÇAISE ET NÉERLANDAISE. (5) LOT 5 : CONCEPTION, MÉDIATISATION, DÉVELOPPEMENT, LIVRAISON, INTEGRATION DANS LA PLATEFORME LMS ERAP AVEC SUPPORT TECHNIQUE ET MAINTENANCE DES DEUX MODULES D’APPRENTISSAGE EN E-LEARNING (CHACUN D’UNE DURÉE ESTIMÉE DE 60 MINUTES) PORTANT RESPECTIVEMENT SUR (1) INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES COMMUNES BRUXELLOISES (2) INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS, EN VERSIONS FRANÇAISE ET NÉERLANDAISE. description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Fight Tonight BAA NUMBER: FA8750-22-S-7001 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA, with a partial Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA for Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2), which is open and effective until 30 Nov 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. title: Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction - NP NER PMS BMS FY24(1)
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for the Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction Project NP NER PMS BMS FY24(1), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000003, located in Dutchess, Nassau, Suffolk and Saratoga Counties, New York; Sullivan County, New Hampshire; and Hampden County, Massachusetts. The project consists of bridge maintenance and pavement preservation of roadways and parking areas across several parks including Home of FDR National Historic Site (HOFR), Eleanor Roosevelt National Historic Site (ELRO), Vanderbilt Mansion National Historic Site (VAMA), Fire Island National Seashore (FIIS), Saint Gaudens National Historic Park (SAGA), Sagamore Hill National Historic Park (SAHI), Saratoga National Historical Park (SARA) and Springfield Armory National Historical Park (SPAR). The work includes thin lift asphalt overlay, chip seal, crack cleaning and sealing, asphalt concrete pavement patching, pavement markings, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $2,000,000 to $3,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about October 29, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will not be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. PLEASE NOTE For security reasons, individuals requiring access to all government buildings must present a valid photo ID and be escorted to their destination by a Government employee. All visitors attending bid openings are urged to arrive at least 1 hour prior to a scheduled bid opening. All visitors must sign in at the main entrance of the Quantum Park facility and wait to be escorted by a Government employee to Eastern Federal Lands Highway Division (EFLHD) in Suite 200. Visitors must then register with the EFLHD Receptionist. A Government employee will collect all bids. Prior to the bid opening, a Government employee will escort all bidders to the bid opening. Unescorted visitors will be denied entry and no exceptions will be made. Bidders are encouraged to submit bids electronically per the instructions provided in the solicitation.

Zamawiający wskazuje, że z uwagi na okoliczności techniczne, organizacyjne roboczogodziny mogą zostać wykorzystane w mniejszym wymiarze, tj. w wymiarze zamówienia podstawowego czyli 110 roboczogodzin. W przypadku nie skorzystania przez Zamawiającego z prawa zlecenia rozbudowy i modyfikacji CMS w wymiarze większym niż 110 roboczogodzin, Wykonawca nie będzie wnosił żadnych roszczeń z tego tytułu. 2. Spełnianie wymogów WCAG na poziomie wymaganym zgodnie z obowiązującymi przepisami prawa (w tym m.in. Ustawy z dnia 4 kwietnia 2019 r. o dostępności cyfrowej stron internetowych i aplikacji mobilnych podmiotów publicznych, Rozporządzenia Rady Ministrów z dnia 12 kwietnia 2012 r. w sprawie Krajowych Ram Interoperacyjności, minimalnych wymagań dla rejestrów publicznych i wymiany informacji w postaci elektronicznej oraz minimalnych wymagań dla systemów teleinformatycznych, Ustawy z dnia 19 lipca 2019 r. o zapewnianiu dostępności osobom ze szczególnymi potrzebami). 3. Ze względu na specyfikę przedmiotu zamówienia Zamawiający przewiduje obowiązek dokonania przez Wykonawcę sprawdzenia dokumentów niezbędnych do realizacji zamówienia, udostępnionych w siedzibie Zamawiającego, zgodnie z zapisami pkt VIII Opisu przedmiotu zamówienia (OPZ) stanowiącego Załącznik nr 3 do SWZ. buyer: VZW Vlaams Centrum voor Agro- en Visserijmarketing
title: Belgium – Advertising and marketing services – European Potato Promotion Campaign
description: From 2020 to 2025, VLAM, CNIPT, Bord Bia and Europatat collaborated on the European fresh potato promotion campaign “Potatoes, prepare to be surprised – Europe’s favourite since 1536”. Building on this experience, the four organisations are joining forces for a new three-year information and promotion campaign, co-funded by the European Union. The new campaign offers an opportunity to develop a fresh and distinctive creative concept. While lessons from the previous campaign can serve as inspiration, we expect an original, new approach, without being bound by the branding, slogan or visual identity of the previous campaign. The new campaign wants to stimulate the consumption of fresh potatoes at EU level and more specifically in three countries, i.e. Belgium (Flanders), France and Ireland. Target group of the campaign is people between 25 and 44 years old The communication objective of the new campaign is to highlight the ease of use (convenience) and versatility of fresh potatoes (pleasure) and their place in a contemporary lifestyle and a healthy, balanced and sustainable diet. The campaign activities include a mix of promotional activities, some implemented in all target countries, others in 1 or more target countries. Common activities include the design of a common look & feel, website, social media template and video. Local activities include collaboration with influencers and creation of local social media posts and/or videos. Our target group will be reached via a multi-channel approach, with a focus on video and social media advertising in all countries. This approach will be extended with native advertising in Flanders and Ireland and PR activities in France.

description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for the Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction, Project NP NER PMS BMS FY25(2), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000004, located in Essex County, New Jersey; Pike, Wayne, and Lackawanna Counties, Pennsylvania; and the City of Baltimore, Maryland. The project consists of roadway and bridge maintenance at Thomas Edison National Historical Park (EDIS), Fort McHenry National Monument and Historic Shrine (FOMC), Steamtown National Historic Site (STEA), and Upper Delaware Scenic and Recreational River (UPDE). The work includes micro surfacing, thin lift asphalt overlay, crack cleaning and sealing, asphalt concrete pavement patching, milling and overlay, concrete repair, drainage repairs, speed bump replacement, concrete paver installation, pavement markings, minor bridge repairs, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $3,000,000 to $4,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about November 6, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. description: Objets des services du marché : DEVELOPPEMENT DE PROGRAMMES ET DE MODULES DE FORMATION EN E-LEARNING DANS LES THEMATIQUES DES MARCHES PUBLICS ET DE L’ORGANISATION FINANCIERE DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. Le marché public est divisé en lots. Les soumissionnaires sont libres d’introduire une offre pour un ou pour plusieurs lots. L’ensemble des lots organisés par le présent marché visent à l’élaboration, la conception technique, la médiatisation, le développement, la livraison, l’intégration avec support technique dans la plateforme LMS de l’ERAP ainsi que la maintenance de trois modules de formation/apprentissage au format e-learning, disponibles simultanément en versions française et néerlandaise. Les lots 1, 2 et 3 visent l’élaboration de trois programmes d’apprentissage (objectifs, contenus, dispositif pédagogique) rendus disponibles en langue française et destinés à s’intégrer dans des modules en e-learning. Ces 3 programmes portent sur les trois thématiques suivantes : - « Introduction aux achats publics des administrations communales et des CPAS bruxellois ». - « Introduction à l’organisation financière des administrations communales bruxelloises ». - « Introduction à l’organisation financière des CPAS bruxellois ». Les lots 4 et 5 visent la conception technique, la médiatisation, le développement technique et la maintenance des trois modules de formation au format e-learning sur base des trois programmes d’apprentissage susmentionnés. Hébergement des modules e-learning : les modules de formation e-learning seront hébergés sur la plateforme LMS de l’ERAP (voir description technique en annexe). Le cas échéant, les modules e-learning seront hébergés sur la plateforme LMS d’un ou plusieurs administrations clientes ou sur un site Internet. Il est à noter que le présent marché ne couvre pas les services liés à l’intégration des modules e-learning sur d’autres plateformes que celle mise à disposition par l’ERAP. Durée des modules e-learning : Les modules de formation au format e-learning visés par les lots 4 et 5 ont une durée respective estimée à 60 minutes (2 x 30 min. ou 4 x 15 min.). Thématique des modules : Ces modules s’intègrent dans un parcours de formation plus large destiné à l’onboarding des agents de niveau A, B ou C des administrations communales et des CPAS de la Région de Bruxelles-capitale. Estimation du nombre d’utilisateurs finaux pour chacun des trois modules d’apprentissage : environ 550 personnes par an (500 apprenants/utilisateurs finaux et 50 responsables représentants les administrations concernées + personnel ERAP). Durée du marché : pour tous les lots, le marché est conclu pour une durée d’un an, renouvelable trois fois pour la même durée, pour une durée totale de 4 ans (voir point II.7 pour les détails). Le marché est divisé en lots de la manière suivante : (1) LOT 1 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION AUX ACHATS PUBLICS DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (3) LOT 3 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». title: NJ-NY ERFO FW WARI 2019-1(1) - Wallkill River National Wildlife Refuge
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for Wallkill River National Wildlife Refuge, Project NJ-NY ERFO FW WARI 2019-1(1), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000005, located in Sussex County, New Jersey; and Orange County, New York. The project consists of repairs to the Winding Waters Trail, Liberty Loop Trail (NE), Liberty Loop Trail (SW), and Dagmar Dale Nature Trail. The work includes embankment repairs, trail reconstruction, culvert replacement, stream regrading, headwall and wingwall installation, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $3,000,000 to $5,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about November 12, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will not be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. title: Strategic Technology Office-wide Innovation Solutions Opening Announcement
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) anticipates funding a limited number of proposals under this solicitation. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. Proposed research should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. The Strategic Technology Office (STO) at DARPA regularly publishes solicitations requesting responses to specific program topics. This announcement seeks revolutionary research ideas for topics not addressed by ongoing STO programs or other published DARPA solicitations. To avoid proposals that duplicate existing activities or are responsive to other published STO solicitations, potential proposers are highly encouraged to review current STO programs and solicitations, respectively listed at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/offices/sto and http://www.darpa.mil/work-with-us/opportunities. Contacting STO program managers to discuss their research interests is also encouraged. A current list of program managers is available at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/people. This Innovation Solutions Opening solicits under the procurement authorities of 10 U.S. Code � 4001, 10 U.S.C. � 4021, 10 U.S.C. � 4022, and 10 U.S.C. � 4023, that allow procurement activities authority to enter into agreements with industry, academia, and other organizations to fund research and development through cooperative agreements, Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research, OTAs for prototypes, and procurement for experimental purposes. Proposals received as a result of this Innovation Solutions Opening will be evaluated by the Government in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified herein through a scientific review process. DARPA solicitations are posted on the SAM website under the Contract Opportunities link at https://sam.gov/. The following information is for those wishing to respond to the Innovation Solutions Opening. 1.1. STO MISSION AND THRUST AREAS DARPA's STO is a systems warfare office that seeks innovative and disruptive technologies for existing and future battlespaces. STO programs deliver solutions at speed and scale for today's warfighters while developing the resilient "breakthrough" systems and technologies across all physical domains (Air, Space, Sea, and Land) and across the spectrum of competition. STO does not focus on one area of responsibility or phenomenology. Instead, STO programs capture the strategic, logistical, and tactical complexity of today's national security environments. description: **AMENDMENT 001 - An attachment has been added. The document contains questions and answers related to the Challenge.** *Please note that the ISC website will be available on October 30th, 2026 as of 10:30am ET. This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en. Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal. Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/artificial-intelligence-ai-decision-making-process-visibility-traceability-and-compliance-governance Challenge title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) decision-making process visibility, traceability and compliance governance Challenge sponsor: Shared Services Canada (SSC) Funding Mechanism: Contract MAXIMUM CONTRACT VALUE: Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. Phase 2: • The maximum funding available for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is : $2,000,000.00 CAD excluding applicable taxes, shipping, travel and living expenses, as required. • The maximum duration for any Phase 2 contracts resulting from this Challenge is up to 20 months (excluding submission of the final report). • Estimated number of Phase 2 contracts: 1 This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to award any contract for the total approximate funding. Final decisions on the number of Phase 1 and Phase 2 (amend as applicable) awards will be made by Canada on the basis of factors such as evaluation results, departmental priorities and availability of funds. Canada reserves the right to make partial awards and to negotiate project scope changes. Note: Selected companies are eligible to receive one contract per phase per challenge. Travel: No travel required. Kick-off Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Progress Review Meeting(s): Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference. Final Review Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Problem Statement: Challenge Statement Summary The Government of Canada (GoC) is committed to the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) compliant with its AI Strategy and Guiding Principles, see references noted in this challenge notice. The widespread adoption of AI technologies has created opportunities to enhance decision-making and improve service delivery within the GoC. In fostering the responsible usage of AI, the GoC has established an adoption strategy and guiding principles. To support adherence and implementation, the GoC is interested in testing solutions that provide visibility into AI decision-making processes, enhance the traceability of AI outputs, and ensure that AI models comply with Canadian laws and international standards and best practices. Despite the availability of AI governance solutions from Canadian companies and international providers, existing offerings typically require significant manual effort. This effort is particularly evident in interpreting evolving AI governance requirements, applying them to specific AI systems, updating controls and assessments, and identifying their ecosystem-wide impacts. The challenge seeks innovation to advance capabilities for identifying and incorporating evolving governance requirements, determining their potential impact on registered AI systems, associated controls, assessments, and evidence, and supporting timely reassessment, all while maintaining explainability, traceability, auditability, and human oversight. Details: Essential (mandatory) Outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Support the continuous alignment of registered AI systems with relevant Canadian regulations, policies, directives, and other governance requirements and be able to identify potentially affected systems and indicate when a reassessment is required. 2. Demonstrate interoperability with enterprise systems, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) platforms and governance solutions and the solution can be integrated with minimal customization. 2A. Demonstrate the ability to exchange governance information with enterprise systems and AI/ML lifecycle tools through standards-based Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), connectors and interoperable data exchange mechanisms. Governance information may include AI system metadata, risk assessments, compliance findings, audit evidence, monitoring results, approvals and decision records. As an example: This governance information includes but is not limited to, information about the AI system, ownership, intent, deployment status, funding state, client information, system objectives, assessments, algorithmic impact assessment, control requirements (playbooks). 2B. title: Solicitation of a Concession Business Opportunity to Operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services within Lake Mead National Recreation Area
description: The National Park Service (NPS) has released on September 2, 2026, a business opportunity soliciting proposals to award a new ten (10) year concession contract to operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services in Lake Mead National Recreation Area. The NPS will host a site visit for entities interested in bidding on the opportunity on September 21, 2026. The site visit provides interested entities with an overview of the concession operation and a tour of the Concession Facilities (land and real property improvements assigned to the concessioner under the Draft Contract), as well as the Desert Princess vessel, which is government-owned personal property assigned to the concessioner. Site Visit Registration Registration is required to attend the site visit. To register, contact Nicole Williams, Concessions Management Specialist, Lake Mead National Recreation Area at nicole_williams@nps.gov, along with a courtesy copy to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov, no later than 12:00 pm (Pacific Time) on September 17, 2026. You must provide your name, contact information, the name of the entity interested in submitting a proposal that you represent, the primary contact for the entity, and the number and names of people in your party. Due to space constraints, the NPS limits the number of site visit attendees to a total of five (5) people per interested entity. Site visit participants are responsible for obtaining their lodging, meals, and transportation to the Concession Facilities. The operation is located at 490 Horsepower Cove, Boulder City, NV 89005. Attendance at the site visit is encouraged, but not required, to submit a proposal. The NPS will not answer questions about this prospectus or business opportunity during registration or the site visit. Interested entities must submit questions in writing after the release of the prospectus to the contact person and by the deadline that will be provided in the prospectus. Interested entities are asked not to interfere with concessioner operations during the site visit and not to film, record or photograph concessioner employees or concessioner operations. Questions Due Questions regarding the prospectus must be received, in writing, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on September 30, 2026. Email your questions to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov. Notice of Intent to Propose Any interested party intending to submit a proposal must submit a "Notice of Intent to Propose" as described in the Business Opportunity and Proposal Instructions, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on November 23, 2026. Submission of Electronic Proposal The NPS is ONLY accepting electronic proposals in response to this prospectus. Any proposal must be received electronically, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on December 22, 2026, in the format outlined in the Proposal Instructions, to be evaluated for award of the new concession contract. Contact List The prospectus is available on the NPS Commercial Services website (link provided below). If you choose to retrieve a copy of the prospectus, please notify Mark Juretschke at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov so you are placed on the mailing list to receive notifications of any future modifications or correspondence.

title: ATR Plant Protection System (PPS) Seismic Switch Replacement
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), the management and operating contractor for the U.S. Department of Energy-owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified suppliers capable of providing environmentally and seismically qualified seismic switches for use in the Advanced Test Reactor (ATR) Plant Protection System (PPS). The purpose of this EOI is to identify suppliers with the technical capability, quality assurance program, testing facilities, and experience necessary to provide safety-related seismic switch equipment qualified for nuclear applications. This EOI is being issued for market research and acquisition planning purposes and is intended to identify potential suppliers for a future procurement opportunity. The EOI process is used by INL to develop a list of qualified and interested vendors that may be considered for future solicitations. BACKGROUND The ATR Plant Protection System currently utilizes seismic switches to provide a critical reactor protection function. Seismic switches detect ground motion and initiate a reactor scram when predetermined seismic thresholds are exceeded. The existing Kinemetrics Model TS-3A seismic switches are obsolete and have demonstrated performance degradation, resulting in increased reliance on limited spare inventory. Additionally, one seismic switch is currently out of service, placing the PPS in a reduced logic configuration. Replacement with modern, supported equipment is required to restore normal system configuration and ensure long-term reliability and maintainability. SCOPE OF INTEREST BEA seeks information from suppliers capable of providing complete seismic switch solutions meeting the functional, environmental, seismic qualification, testing, documentation, and quality assurance requirements typically associated with nuclear safety-related applications. Functional Capability Three-axis ground motion sensing capability. Dry contact output suitable for reactor protection system input. Adjustable seismic trip setpoints. Response times consistent with nuclear protection system applications. Long-term reliability and maintainability. In-situ testing and calibration capabilities. Environmental and Seismic Qualification Respondents should be capable of qualifying equipment consistent with applicable industry standards, including IEEE 603 IEEE 323 IEEE 344 ANSI/ISA-67.04.01 ASME NQA-1 Deliverables Suppliers should be capable of providing: Complete seismic switch assemblies. Required mounting hardware and accessories. Qualification documentation and test reports. Operation and maintenance manuals. Installation and interface documentation. Calibration and surveillance procedures. Certificates of conformance and applicable certifications. MINIMUM MANDATORY CAPABILITIES To facilitate evaluation, respondents should clearly identify whether they can meet the following minimum capabilities: Provide a seismic switch solution capable of detecting low-level seismic events suitable for reactor protection applications. Demonstrate environmental and seismic qualification in accordance with IEEE 323 and IEEE 344 methodologies. Maintain a Quality Assurance Program consistent with ASME NQA-1 requirements or equivalent controls. Support a qualified service life suitable for long-term nuclear facility operation. Provide qualification reports, testing documentation, calibration information, and supporting quality records. Provide long-term product support, maintenance recommendations, and obsolescence management. RESPONSE FORMAT AND SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested organizations shall submit a concise response demonstrating their qualifications, capabilities, and interest in supporting this requirement. Responses should be limited to approximately 10 pages, excluding product literature, drawings, certifications, and supporting quality documentation. Responses should include, at a minimum: Organization name, mailing address, and primary point of contact UEI and CAGE Code (if applicable) Business size and socio-economic classifications Technical capabilities Relevant experience Quality Assurance Program information Manufacturing and delivery capabilities Estimated lead times Assumptions, exceptions, or recommendations related to the requirement Responses shall be submitted electronically in PDF format to: Chase Egbert & Stacey Hill Email: Chase.Egbert@inl.gov and Stacey.Hill@inl.gov Responses must be received no later than: April 23, 2027 PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents should clearly identify any proprietary or confidential information contained within their submission. DISCLAIMER This Expression of Interest (EOI) is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or commitment by BEA or INL to procure supplies or services. BEA reserves the right to use information received through this EOI to evaluate market capabilities, acquisition strategies, and potential supplier interest. Submission of an EOI response does not guarantee participation in any future solicitation and does not obligate BEA or INL to award a contract. BEA is not responsible for any costs incurred by respondents in preparing or submitting responses to this EOI. Information obtained through this process may be used to assist in developing future procurement requirements and solicitation strategies

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND NEXT GENERATION DISTRIBUTED COMMAND AND CONTROL
description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror�s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Gennady Staskevich AFRL/RISC 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330-4889 Email: gennady.staskevich@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. No other changes are made. PLEASE SEE ATTACHMENT FOR FULL AMENDMENT DETAILS. Section IV.2; updates the Content and Format language; Section VI.3, updates the debriefing language; Section VI.7; updates the provisions; Section VII; updates the OMBUDSMAN No other changes are made. description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror�s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement.
