While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror�s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. title: Netherlands, Germany – Industry specific software development services – Expertise for the Control Room of the Future program (Dynamic Purchasing System - EU-404)
description: Welcome to the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for Expertise for the Control Room of the Future program and adjacent subjects. Note: This Dynamic Purchasing System is a continuation on the Mercell platform of the DPS that was previously operational on the Negometrix platform with Negometrix reference 159478 for which formal notice 2021/S 087-226573 was published on 5-May-2021 on the TED website. If your company was already qualified for participation on the Negometrix platform, a simplified procedure applies for re-establishing your qualification, see question 2.1 on the Mercell platform. TenneT will renew and innovate the (IT) systems that it uses for controlling and balancing its grids in the period 2021-2031. In connection with this, TenneT expects to be needing extensive external expertise, related to existing and new technologies and ways of working, in particular related to the challenges that TenneT faces in the energy transition. Compared to current ways of working, innovations will be needed to handle e.g. the increasing infeed of solar and wind energy that is far more difficult to predict and control than traditional generation. The subject of this tender procedure is a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for expertise (including the development of algorithms and IT Tools) that TenneT needs in connection with the renewal of its (IT) systems related to the control and balancing of the electricity transmission grid. Initially, the DPS contains the following categories of expertise: 1. power system control and monitoring; 2. energy platforms and interconnected IT systems; 3. data analysis, artificial intelligence and machine learning; 4. system and process implementation. This Tender Dossier contains the rules for the Application by Economic operators for qualification under this DPS. In order to become qualified for one or more of the categories, the Economic operator has to fulfil all the requirements of this DPS. In addition, the Economic operator needs to the answer all Mercell questions, and submit the requested documents and-or evidence at the respective Mercell question with the submission of its Application. During the course of time, the specific assignments (contracts) under the DPS will be tendered for which all suppliers that have qualified for the particular category will be invited to submit an offer. Any interested supplier may at any moment during the lifetime of the DPS submit a request to be qualified for participating in the tender procedures for specific assignments within one or more of the categories of this DPS. Your request will be accepted if it satisfies the applicable requirements and if you accept the stated conditions. Once you have qualified, you will automatically receive a notification when TenneT publishes a request for proposal for a specific subject within a category for which you have qualified. TenneT emphasises that it would also like to attract small and medium sized companies to this DPS. Qualification requests will be processed by TenneT in the sequence of receipt. TenneT will inform you as soon as possible and endeavors to do so within 10 working days from the date of receipt about the acceptance or rejection of your qualification request. During the lifetime of the DPS, TenneT will be entitled to add new categories, to close existing categories, and to split-up existing categories in to one or more categories.

title: Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YON-325
description: The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF) is conducting market research to determine industry capability and interest in performing the maintenance, repair, and preservation of YON-325. Work will be accomplished at the Contractor's facility. The Government is seeking responses from sources that can perform the following work. Geographical Area of consideration: To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. YON-325 � Length: 199 FT � Width: 54 FT � Height: 15 FT � Age: 21 YRS � Hull Type: Steel � Draft: 3 FT � Full Displacement: 2,848 L Tons � Light Load: 706 L Tons Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) to deliver the vessel from Manchester Fuel Depot to the Contractor�s facility. Dock, wash, and clean exterior surfaces of the vessel upon docking. Replace zinc anodes on hull / Skegs. Accomplish preservation to Underwater Hull, Freeboard, Main deck, Deck house, Cargo piping and all deck fittings. Clean non-skid located Main deck, Deck house top and Cargo deck. Remove, clean and install Rubber fenders. Modify existing Piping eliminate Aft Flow Meter and insert spool. Accomplish Ultrasonic test measurement and visual inspection of the hull, Main deck, Cargo deck and Deck house top. Open, Clean, Pump and maintain clean and dry each tank/void. Inspect tanks/voids for defects Refresh Exhaust Muffler for Yanmar and Main Engine. Replace Solar Panels. Remove Antenna Support Modification. Replace Fuel Oil Tank Piping. Replace and Calibrate Cargo Tank Level Indicator�s (TLI�s). Perform Preliminary Air test of Tanks/voids/Steel Fendering and Skegs. Accomplish a final closure inspection of each tank/void upon completion of all work installing new gaskets and fasteners. Perform Final Air Test of Tanks/voids/Steel Fendering and Skegs. Accomplish repair, replace gaskets, and adjust watertight hatches and doors. Accomplish Cargo Pump Diesel and Diesel generator maintenance and repair. Undock the vessel. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the COR. Calibration of TLI�s, shall be conducted at Manchester Fuel Depot (MFD) in Manchester, WA. YON-325 Prime Period of Performance: Estimated August 2027 through November 2027 What/Where to Submit: Interested companies should submit, on company letterhead, a notice of interest including the name, telephone number, mailing address, and e-mail address of one point of contact. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) anticipates the need for a firm-fixed-price construction contract for a project entitled Repair Security Wall, at the United States Penitentiary (USP) Lewisburg, located in Lewisburg, Pennsylvania. The project consists of the following: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP), United States Penitentiary (USP) Lewisburg, intends to make a single award to a responsible entity that will provide all necessary equipment, labor, materials, and incidentals necessary to repair the concrete security wall and associated expansion joints, inspect and repair brick column assemblies located at expansion joints along the perimeter concrete security wall. The work is required to restore structural stability, prevent deterioration, and maintain perimeter security standards. All work shall be performed in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local codes, Bureau of Prisons (BOP) policies, and recognized industry standards for structural concrete repair. SCOPE OF WORK (WALL RESTORATION): TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS Wall Repair Activities Expansion Joint Repair Activities Brick Column Assembly Repair Pre-Cast Concrete Cap Replacement See the Statement of Work/Specifications attachment for the complete requirements for the project. Access to the specifications and drawings attachments will require an active https://sam.gov vendor registration (log in). If you encounter problems accessing these documents, please contact the Federal Service Desk at 866-606-8220. Interested contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://sam.gov. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 238140 (Masonry Contractors) with a corresponding small business standard at $19.0 million average annual receipts for the firms preceding three fiscal years. The estimated magnitude of this project lies between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. Interested bidders must be registered in https://sam.gov. The FBOP is seeking small business contractors for this project. Your business size metrics information entered in your SAM registration must be less than or equal to the small business size standard specified above to qualify as a small business. Interested contractors are requested to respond to this notice by adding their names to the Interested Vendors List for this posting on the SAM website at https://sam.gov. You must be logged in to your vendor account in order to access the Interested Vendors List. Please add your business name only if you are interested in submitting an offer as a Prime contractor and are capable and eligible to compete for and perform this project. This notice is intended only for those who would be entering into a Prime contract with the FBOP for the entirety of the project. The FBOP has no privity of contract with subcontractors. Interested small business contractors are requested to respond to this notice by filling out and emailing completed questionnaire attachment to Kevin Slone at kslone@bop.gov. Responses must be received by November 19, 2026. Interested vendors must also add their name to the Interested Vendors List for this posting in https://sam.gov Contract Opportunity (must be logged-in to your vendor account). The synopsis of proposed contract action will include further instructions for responding to this opportunity. Interested offerors are advised to continuously monitor SAM for all future updates.

title: France – Advertising and marketing services – Prestations de communication numérique touristique et d'attractivité-.
description: Le présent marché a pour objet la structuration et la planification d’une communication numérique dédiée à la promotion des atouts touristiques de Troyes Champagne Métropole. Cette stratégie doit reposer principalement sur un vécu expérientiel dans lequel les prospects et repeaters (visiteurs récurrents) vont se projeter et s’identifier. Pour ce faire, les prestations attendues au titre de ce marché reposent sur une stratégie de promotion numérique sur Internet et les réseaux sociaux (dont ceux de l’Office du tourisme, de la ville de Troyes et de Troyes Champagne Métropole) et pouvant être déclinés en spots télévisés segmentés et replay. Conformément à l’article L2113-10 du Code de la commande publique, la présente consultation est allotie comme suit : Lot n°1 : Création et mise au format de visuels publicitaires ; Lot n°2 : Réalisation de vidéos et prise de photos ; Lot n°3 : Média planning et stratégie de diffusion numérique ; En application de l’article R2113-1 du Code de la commande publique, les opérateurs économiques peuvent soumissionner pour les 3 lots. Les 3 lots susvisés peuvent être attribués à un seul et même opérateur économique. Conformément aux dispositions des articles L2125-1.1°, R. 2162-1 à R. 2162-6 et R. 2162-13 à R. 2162-14 du Code de la Commande Publique, chaque lot donnera lieu, à la conclusion d’un accord-cadre mono-attributaire à bons de commande. Le titulaire de l’accord-cadre sera consulté, à chaque survenance d’un besoin, par le biais de l’émission de bons de commande, conformément aux dispositions des articles R. 2162-13 et R. 2162-14 du Code de la Commande Publique. En application de l’article R.2162-4-2° du Code de la Commande Publique, l’accord-cadre sera conclu avec les montants maximum suivants : - S’agissant du lot n°1 : un montant maximum de 40 000 € HT annuel ; - S’agissant du lot n°2 : un montant maximum de 60 000 € HT annuel ; - S’agissant du lot n°3 : un montant maximum de 80 000 € HT annuel. Pour chaque lot, la durée de validité du présent marché court à compter de sa date de notification pour une durée d’un an. Celui-ci est reconductible, 3 fois par voie tacite, par période de 12 mois. Le titulaire du marché public ne pourra refuser la reconduction conformément aux dispositions de l’article R2112-4 du Code de la commande publique. En cas de non-reconduction, un courrier sera adressé au(x) titulaire(s) du marché public au moins un mois avant l’échéance de ce dernier. Pour chaque lot, les délais d’exécution seront fixés au sein de chaque bon de commande.

title: FEMA Request for Information - Direct Housing Modernization Capabilities
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulations Overhaul (RFO) 15.101(c). This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Quotation (RFQ), and it is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to enter into a contract, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response to this request. All information contained in this RFI is preliminary and is subject to change if, and when, a solicitation is issued. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. If a competitive solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) website. It is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this RFI, or future solicitations. The Department of Homeland Security, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Office of Direct Housing Operations, is conducting market research to identify and seek capabilities from industry in five primary functional areas: Automated Real Estate Aggregation and Vacancy Sourcing - Automated discovery and ingestion of residential rental property listings via Multiple Listing Services (MLS), property management software APIs, commercial rental boards, and direct landlord entry portals. - Real-time vacancy validation to prevent matching against obsolete or unavailable listings. - Rapid geo-fencing within disaster-declared zones and surrounding reasonable-commute perimeters. Artificial Intelligence and Algorithmic Matching - Multi-constraint matching algorithms that pair applicant household profiles with available properties in seconds. - Multi-point geospatial proximity optimization factoring in school district retention, work commutes, medical/provider travel distance, and essential services. - Household composition sizing aligned with HUD Housing Quality Standards (HQS) and FEMA occupancy guidelines. Automated Physical Accessibility Verification - Algorithmic filtering and computer vision inspection tools capable of evaluating floor plans, entry photos, and property specifications against UFAS and ADA physical accessibility standards. - Rapid identification of barrier-free environments, ramps, ground-floor units, grab bars, and wheelchair-accessible kitchens and bathrooms. Landlord Engagement and Leasing Workflow Automation - Automated outreach tools and self-service portals for landlords to submit properties, accept lease terms, and coordinate inspections. - Integration with standard government lease templates and automated electronic signature workflows. Secure Federal Architecture - Enterprise data security architecture compliant with the Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) at the Moderate impact baseline. - FedRAMP-authorized cloud hosting (or capability to achieve FedRAMP Moderate/High authorization). - Strict data protection for Sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) belonging to disaster survivors. NAICS CODE: 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services) / 531210 (Offices of Real Estate Agents and Brokers) PRODUCT SERVICE CODE (PSC): X1FA, Lease/Rental of Family Housing Facilities ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE START DATE: TBD RFI RESPONSE SUBMITTAL INSTRUCTIONS: Interested contractors shall submit Questions and RFI responses electronically to the Contracting Officer, at Rachel.Woods@fema.dhs.gov no later than 12:00PM Eastern Time (ET), December 18, 2026. Phone calls will not be accepted. Please see the attachment for further instructions and information.

title: Utilities Privatization of the Water System at U.S. Army Garrison-Hawaii (USAG-HI), Island of Oahu
description: DLA Energy, in conjunction with the United States Army, plans to offer the privatization of the Water distribution (NAICS 221310) utility system at U.S. Army Garrison-Hawaii, Island of Oahu. Utilities Privatization (UP) is defined as the transfer of ownership and responsibility to a municipal, private, regional, district, or cooperative utility company or other entity, for the operations, maintenance, repair, future upgrades, and future utility systems replacements. The conveyance may consist of all right, title, and interest of the United States in the utility system. UP will be accomplished in accordance with 10 U.S.C. �2688 � Utility Systems: Conveyance Authority. As a result of this solicitation, the Contractor(s) will be selected to assume ownership of the Water utility system. The new owner(s) shall operate and maintain the system and provide utility services to the Government. Any resulting contract, if awarded, will require the Contractor to furnish all facilities, labor, materials, tools, and equipment necessary to own, maintain, and operate the utility system. All responsibility for maintaining reliable service, including such items as environmental compliance, maintenance costs, major system renovations, construction, equipment, manpower, and overhead costs shall become the utility system owner�s responsibility. The Contractor shall manage the maintenance, repairs, replacement, etc., of the system to ensure continuous, adequate, and dependable service for each Government or tenant connection within the service area. The Contractor shall be responsible for funding all capital investments required to acquire, maintain, and operate the utility system in a safe, reliable condition and to meet the requirements listed in the contract. Real property interests will be conveyed in the form of a Right to Access or an Easement as a reference to the resultant contract. The utility system will be conveyed via a Bill of Sale after a transition period to be determined by the Contractor. Past performance information from potential offerors shall be submitted as directed in the solicitation. A Sources Sought Notice for this requirement was previously publicized under solicitation number SP060026R0813 on May 29, 2026. The Sources Sought Notice has closed and market research is complete. This requirement will be unrestricted. All responsible sources are encouraged to submit an offer. Other-than-small businesses are required to submit a subcontracting plan with their offer. Interested sources may contact Jonathan Moore, Contracting Officer at jonathan.moore@dla.mil, Timothy Stark, Contracting Officer at timothy.1.stark@dla.mil, Kathryn Bowman, Contract Specialist at kathryn.bowman@dla.mil, and Lexy Sweitzer, Contract Specialist, at lexy.sweitzer@dla.mil to be added to our offeror mailing list. In order to view those documents, vendors will need to obtain special access. The process of obtaining access is somewhat lengthy, therefore all interested vendors are encouraged to begin that process as soon as possible. Instructions for obtaining access are provided below. Should any party have issues with obtaining access to SAM.gov or the secure documents, they must notify the contracting office no later than September 29, 2026. Current mission command systems are not mobile, intuitive, or survivable enough to easily overcome the current threat, changes in the character of warfare, and the pace of technology. As part of the Army�s continuous transformation effort, initiatives are being implemented to transform how the Army operates, trains, and equips for C2 capabilities that enhance its lethality, mobility, and survivability in large-scale combat as part of the Joint Force. The Army�s operational imperative is to improve systems responsibly, using innovative solutions from units and industry; at the same time, preparing for the future by ensuring the next generation of C2 systems are built on a portfolio of capabilities that effectively address emerging threats and ensure dominance over adversaries. The Army�s Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) portfolio of capabilities will provide commanders with the ability to make more, better, and faster decisions through advanced analytics, an integrated data layer, open architecture, and robust and resilient transport. The result is data-centric C2 at every echelon that can operate in any environment. NGC2 requirements are currently being informed by persistent experimentation. Market research and prototyping will create a competitive environment for innovative industry partnerships and continuous integration of new technologies. Army Contracting Command- Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG) in support of the Program Executive Office Command, Control, Communications and Network (PEO C3N) and the Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) program is publishing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), W15P7T-25-S-0001, in accordance with the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement Subpart 212.70 for the purpose of establishing a streamlined vehicle to award innovative C2 capability and functionality. This CSO will remain open until 16 May 2027. This CSO will be open until canceled by the U.S. Army. title: Netherlands – Research and development consultancy services – DAS Innovatie- en adviesdiensten
description: De gemeente Den Haag staat voor steeds complexere maatschappelijke opgaven, die vragen om nieuwe oplossingen, innovatieve werkwijzen en aanvullende expertise. Om hier adequaat op in te kunnen spelen, investeren verschillende domeinen en diensten binnen de Gemeente in innovatie en in het versterken van het eigen innovatievermogen. Bij de ontwikkeling en uitvoering van innovatieprocessen bestaat regelmatig behoefte aan aanvullende, specialistische expertise en ondersteuning van externe partijen. Deze behoefte kan per vraagstuk, fase van het innovatieproces en organisatieonderdeel verschillen. Om deze expertise op een flexibele, efficiënte en transparante wijze te kunnen inzetten, kiest de Gemeente voor het inrichten van een Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem (DAS). Binnen dit DAS kunnen marktpartijen die voldoen aan de gestelde toelatings- en geschiktheidseisen worden toegelaten en meedingen naar Nadere opdrachten. Het Schuldenlab070 neemt het initiatief tot het inrichten van een Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem (DAS), gericht op de begeleiding en ondersteuning van innovatieprocessen binnen de gehele gemeentelijke organisatie (gemeente Den Haag). Binnen dit DAS kunnen de verschillende domeinen en diensten op afroep en naar behoefte gespecialiseerde innovatiepartijen inschakelen. Doel hiervan is om expertise flexibel in te zetten ter versterking van het eigen innovatievermogen, en om werkzaamheden efficiënter, effectiever en duurzamer uit te voeren. Het uitgangspunt voor de opdrachten die binnen dit DAS worden uitgevraagd, is het innovatieproces zoals gebruikt bij onder andere het Schuldenlab070 en van EC-DISC (expertise Centrum Digitale innovatie en Smart City). Binnen deze processen worden concepten, experimenten en pilots ingericht en gevalideerd volgens een vaste en gefaseerde aanpak. Onder het innovatieproces vallen diverse standaarddiensten ter begeleiding en ondersteuning van innovatie(processen), waaronder bijvoorbeeld: -Probleemanalyse, trendanalyse en Strategische verkenning; -Het faciliteren en begeleiden van processen, werksessies en co-creatietrajecten; -Het begeleiden van de ontwikkeling en uitwerking van innovatieve concepten; -Projectsturing en programmabegeleiding; -Monitoring en evaluatie, waaronder maatschappelijke kosten-batenanalyses (MKBA) en impact- en effectmetingen. Daarnaast worden er regelmatig evenementen georganiseerd en trainingen gegeven die los staan van het innovatieproces. Het DAS is onderverdeeld in verschillende fasen van het innovatieproces. Ten behoeve van de inrichting en uitvoering van het DAS worden deze categorieën in Mercell/TenderNed als percelen weergegeven. Gegadigden dienen bij hun verzoek tot toelating aan te geven voor welke fase(n) zij in aanmerking wensen te komen. Het is toegestaan om zich voor één, meerdere of alle fasen aan te melden, mits wordt voldaan aan de voor die fase geldende eisen. Hoewel de gemeente binnen dit DAS primair opdrachten op het gebied van procesbegeleiding van sociale en fysieke innovatie zal uitzetten, kunnen ook opdracht worden uitgevraagd op het snijvlak van sociale en digitale innovatie. Hierbij kan gedacht worden aan de inzet van Artificial intelligence (AI) en andere digitale technologieën ter ondersteuning van innovatie, dienstverlening en besluitvorming, gericht op het effectiever aanpakken van sociaal-maatschappelijke opgaven. Onder deze DAS vallen dan de procesbegeleiding, maar niet de daadwerkelijke productontwikkeling van de digitale tools of systemen. Vraagstukken waarvan het primaire doel bestaat uit onderzoek, klantreisonderzoek, servicedesign of UX-design vallen niet onder de reikwijdte van dit DAS. Deze vallen namelijk onder de gemeentebrede raamovereenkomst voor de inhuur van Onderzoeks-, Service Design- en User Experience Design (UX)-medewerkers.

title: Germany – Urban planning services – Stadtteil- und Citymanagement
description: Die Schloss-Stadt Hückeswagen setzt nun schon seit mehreren Jahren erfolgreich das Integrierte Stadtentwicklungskonzept (ISEK) um. Ein zentraler Baustein dieser Entwicklung ist das etablierte Citymanagement, das seit Frühjahr 2023 als verbindendes Element zwischen Verwaltung, Politik, Bürgerschaft sowie lokalen Akteur:innen und Gewerbetreibenden wirkt. Es trägt wesentlich zur Transparenz, Kommunikation und aktiven Beteiligung bei und unterstützt die positive Entwicklung der Innenstadt. Die aktuelle Förderphase endet im Jahr 2026. In den darauffolgenden Jahren 2027, 2028 und 2029 stehen jedoch noch weitere zentrale bauliche und funktionale Umgestaltungsmaßnahmen im Innenstadt-bereich an. Diese betreffen insbesondere bedeutende Stadträume und Schlüsselprojekte mit hoher öffentlicher Wahrnehmung. Insbesondere das Leuchtturm-Projekt "Schloss für ALLE!" sowie die Umgestaltung der Altstadtstraßen, die zum Schloss führen werden bis 2028 bzw. 2032 umgesetzt. Alle ISEK-Maßnahmen sind einer Übersichtskarte auf der Projektwebseite zu entnehmen: https://www.zukunfthueckeswagen.de/ Vor dem Hintergrund der Beantragung weiterer Fördermittel erfolgt - vorbehaltlich der Bewilligung durch den Fördermittelgeber - eine erneute Ausschreibung des Projekt- und Citymanagements. Dieses ist erforderlich, um eine kontinuierliche Kommunikation sicherzustellen, Beteiligungsprozesse zu begleiten sowie die Attraktivität des Standorts während der Bauphasen weiterhin zu sichern. Ziel ist es, die bereits angestoßene Entwicklung strategisch weiterzuführen und die Wirkung der getätigten Investitionen nachhaltig zu stärken.

buyer: Agentur für Innovation in der Cybersicherheit GmbH (Cyberagentur)
title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – [AI-as-OS] Artificial Intelligence as Operating System
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have been expanding into new areas of application for years. AI systems are increasingly capable of handling complex tasks with greater autonomy—for example, through agent-based approaches that run an AI agent on a computer to perform any task automatically or even autonomously, sometimes without explicit human instructions but rather based on identified intentions (see, for example, the open-source software OpenClaw, which can handle tasks such as calendar maintenance or file management). Just how deeply AI algorithms and models are now integrated into everyday applications is also evident in the fact that end devices are increasingly operable entirely without visible applications and exclusively via voice control, which fundamentally rethinks the way we interact with them (such as Deutsche Telekom’s AI Phone). The central control units of such end devices—the operating systems themselves—are also increasingly being enhanced with new AI functionalities to continuously improve system efficiency. These include initial theoretical—and in some cases already practical—approaches to using the latest AI technologies for file system or storage management. These developments mark a fundamental paradigm shift: AI is no longer viewed merely as an add-on, but increasingly as a native architectural component of the operating system itself. The AI-as-OS program aims to explore how artificial intelligence can be understood not merely as a separately encapsulated functionality that is simply executed by the operating system, but as the operating system itself—Artificial Intelligence as Operating System. Behind this lies the vision of an AI that not only supports individual applications but also acts as the central control system for the entire computer ecosystem, managing system resources (including the CPU, RAM, and system security) in a data-driven, adaptive, and context-aware manner. The aim of the program is to make fundamental contributions to the development of AI-based operating systems as the control unit of a computer system. Through the extensive integration of AI technologies into deep operating system layers, such a system is intended to manage system resources, enable context-aware operational decisions, and enhance system security through adaptive threat detection and defense. Since the underlying technology is still largely in a speculative stage, the scope of development work ranges from the general architecture of such an operating system to the integration of AI-based core mechanisms, and includes new considerations regarding the security and stability requirements for such an operating system, depending on the target platform (e.g., desktop, data center, edge device) and the application environment. The program’s main areas of research include: • AI-Centric Operating System Architectures: Concepts for the fundamental design of an operating system in which AI is viewed not as an add-on feature but as an integral part of the architecture. • AI-Native Core Mechanisms: Integration of AI-based methods into core operating system functions such as resource management, process control, and memory organization. • Control, Security, and Stability: Requirements for traceability, controllability, and robustness of an AI-based operating system, as well as approaches to adaptive threat detection and defense. From today’s perspective, it remains to be seen whether—and to what extent—the vision of an AI-native operating system can be technically realized. This is precisely where the program’s value lies: AI-as-OS explores a largely speculative field at the intersection of AI research and system software, the results of which could set the course for the operating systems of tomorrow.

buyer: Agentur für Innovation in der Cybersicherheit GmbH
title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – [Ne-Trust] Negative Trust Architectures
description: IT systems face an increasing threat from insiders - individuals who often move through systems undetected, exploring IT infrastructure and causing damage. The growing awareness of this attack vector is further amplified by the use of artificial intelligence (AI). These current and future challenges also extend to the realms of public administration, defense, and security agencies. To be prepared for such threat scenarios, IT security paradigms are of critical importance: they shape the fundamental ways in which IT systems are designed, operated, and protected. "Zero Trust" is the most well-established example; however, as a countermeasure against insider threats, this approach has its limitations. Key foundational documents, such as the NIST SP 800-207 guideline, point to remaining gaps and areas that require further research. Against this backdrop, there is a need to explore an advanced, novel paradigm for more effectively defending against insiders. The goal of "Ne-Trust" is to enable demonstrably better detection and more proactive defense against the evolving and increasingly complex insider threats to IT systems, thereby advancing beyond the Zero Trust model. The program is built upon the innovative concept of "Negative Trust" - a term related to Zero Trust, yet one that can also function as an independent designation for a distinct paradigm. While initial attempts to define "Negative Trust" have been made - for instance, in the context of deception technology - a comprehensive scientific and interdisciplinary examination of the term, aimed at establishing it as a standalone, evolved IT security paradigm, has yet to be conducted. Ne-Trust addresses precisely this gap, creating an opportunity for the first-ever scientific exploration and development of "negative-trust" architectures. In doing so, the Cyber ​​Agency opens the door to novel and disruptive research perspectives, providing early impetus for the cybersecurity paradigms and IT security architectures of the future - and beyond. This forward-looking vision - along with the potential for a quantum leap in the defensive capabilities of IT systems and the comprehensive examination of conceptual, technological, social, and legal issues - underscores both the ambitious and the high-risk nature of this research program.

Dynamisch aankoopsysteem De hierbij gebruikte procedure is het Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem uit de Aanbestedingswet 2012. De procedure verloopt volledig elektronisch via het online aanbestedingsplatform Negometrix. Een Dynamisch aankoopsysteem (DAS) is een elektronisch proces voor het doen van gangbare aankopen van werken, leveringen of diensten, waarvan de kenmerken wegens de algemene beschikbaarheid op de markt voldoen aan onze behoeften. Doelstelling DAS De doelstelling van het DAS is een zo groot mogelijke groep kwalitatief goede ondernemingen toe te laten zonder de beheersbaarheid te verliezen. Op deze manier creëert Defensie een optimale marktwerking, waarbij Defensie kwalitatief optimale Producten kan selecteren tegen zo laag mogelijke kosten, binnen de gewenste levertijden. Het MatlogCo beoogt hiermee op een eerlijke wijze, snel en eenvoudig haar behoeften op te vullen, door middel van volledige concurrentiestelling. Werking van het Dynamisch aankoopsysteem in het kort Voor deze aanbesteding volgt Defensie de Europese aanbestedingsprocedure 'Dynamisch aankoopsysteem', conform de Aanbestedingswet. Hierbij wordt onderscheid gemaakt naar twee fasen: 1. Instellingsfase 2. Gunningsfase Deze fasen worden nader uitgewerkt in vragenlijst 1.1. Kort samengevat Gegadigde dient een Verzoek tot toelating in; Als Gegadigde aan de gestelde eisen voldoet en er geen uitsluitingsgronden van toepassing zijn, wordt zij als Deelnemer toegelaten. Toelating tot het DAS houdt geen opdracht in; Het MatlogCo plaats een nadere uitvraag; Deelnemer schrijft in; Het MatlogCo beoordeelt de Inschrijvingen en gunt aan de economisch meest voordelige Inschrijving. Looptijd van het Dynamisch aankoopsysteem Bij de publicatie in maart 2023 had het Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem (DAS) een initiële looptijd van 48 maanden. Echter, aangezien deze DAS een voortzetting is van de vorige DAS met het negometrix nummer 210681, resteert er nu nog een looptijd van 35 maanden. Het is belangrijk op te merken dat de Aanbestedende Dienst de looptijd één keer kan verlengen, met een periode van 48 maanden. Het staat de Aanbestedende dienst vrij om aan het DAS gedurende de looptijd producten en/of kwalificaties toe te voegen of te verwijderen. Dit zal de Aanbestedende dienst waar nodig aankondigen met een rectificatie.

title: Ireland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Panel for the provision of Architect Led Services for projects of less than €1 million (ex. VAT) in value
description: Dublin City Council is establishing a Panel for the provision of Architectural Services for projects of less than €1 million (ex. VAT) in value. Panel members will be required to provide architectural design and associated services for stages (i)-(v) of the Capital Works Management Framework (CWMF) or a subset thereof. As part of the service delivery, panel members will be required to provide the following minimum specialist services: • Design Team Lead, • Architect, • Employer’s Representative for works contracts, • Design Certifier (under the Building Control Amendment Regulations 2014) • Assigned Certifier (under the Building Control Amendment Regulations 2014) • PSDP Additional optional specialist services that may be required include Measured Surveys; Condition Surveys; Architectural Conservation Consultancy Services; Accessibility Audits; Design Services for Disability Access Certificates and Fire Safety Consultancy Services. It is intended that the architectural services to be provided will cover the following project types: feasibility studies, residential (new build and refurbishment), public realm, precinct improvements, housing, civic, community, recreational, sports, infrastructural improvement master-planning, mixed use/commercial etc. The services will cover any and all (CWMF) work stages. Only those Applicants capable of delivering all of the minimum specialist services listed above (whether in-house or as a grouping/consortium) will be considered. Therefore, applications relating to one or several of these services only are not acceptable and will be rejected Every effort has been made to ensure that this document contains all the necessary information for the completion of applications. The Contracting Authority does not warrant or represent that this document, or any other information given to Applicants, is accurate or complete. No liability is accepted for any error, misstatement, or omission (negligent or otherwise) in this document, or in any other information given to Applicants. Requests for additional information and clarification on any matters must be made by email via .www.etenders.gov.ie under CfT ID 6990551. Any additional information will be made available to all potential Applicants who have noted their interest on the eTenders website (www.etenders.gov.ie). It is expected that the Panel will be active in December 2025. Deadline for applications is 1/12/25 at 12pm noon.

title: Finland – Training and entertainment software development services – HAUS DPS 2026–2030 for Digital Transformation, Innovation and Public Sector Development
description: HAUS Finnish Institute of Public Management Ltd (HAUS) is establishing a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for the period 2026–2030 for the procurement of expert services related to digital transformation, innovation, governance, institutional development and public sector development. The estimated total value of procurements conducted under the DPS during its validity period is approximately EUR 40 million (excluding VAT). The DPS will be used to procure expertise for international development cooperation projects, technical assistance assignments, advisory services, capacity building initiatives, studies, evaluations and other expert services implemented globally. Assignments may be funded by, among others, the European Union, the Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland, development finance institutions and other international cooperation partners. The DPS is divided into the following categories: 1. Digital Transformation, Data, Artificial Intelligence & Cybersecurity 2. Governance, Public Sector Development & Capacity Building 3. Innovation, Investment Readiness & Technical Assistance 4. Communications, Media, Creative & Visibility Services The DPS is open to suppliers from Finland and internationally. Suppliers may apply to one or several categories and, once admitted, will have the opportunity to participate in mini-competitions launched throughout the DPS period 2026–2030. Further information regarding the scope, eligibility requirements and application process is provided in the procurement documents.

title: Netherlands – Supply services of personnel including temporary staff – DAS geëxploiteerd door Werken in Noord-Holland Noord
description: U kunt inschrijven op Inhuurdesk Werken in Noord-Holland Noord Inhuur van tijdelijk personeel De gemeente Schagen maakt per 26 september 2026 voor de inhuur van tijdelijk personeel gebruik van Inhuurdesk Werken in Noord-Holland Noord Conform de nieuwe richtlijnen voor de Aanbestedingswet 2012 is deze inhuurdesk ingericht als Dynamisch Aankoop Systeem (DAS) voor de categorieën: Administratief/secretarieel Automatisering/ICT/GEO/Gis Bestuurlijk Binnendienst/algemene dienst Bouwkunde & Civiele techniek Buitendienst & Groenvoorziening Burger- en publiekszaken Dienstverlening & Facilitair Financieel & Economisch Gezondheidszorg Griffie Hydrologie/ ecologie Juridisch Management & Bedrijfsvoering Onderwijs Openbare Orde en Veiligheid Personeel & Organisatie Ruimtelijke ordening & Milieu Sociale zaken & Werkgelegenheid Sport & Recreatie Techniek (E, WTB, Proces) Vergunning & Handhaving Verkeer & Vervoer Verkoop & Inkoop Voorlichting & Communicatie Welzijn Wetenschap & Cultuur. Deze categorieën zijn het totaal van alle door de aangesloten organisatie gebruikte categorieën. De aangesloten organisatie behoudt zich het recht voor om op een later moment categorieën toe te voegen of te wijzigen. Toevoegingen en/of wijzigingen zullen worden gepubliceerd op Mercell , TenderNed en de website van gemeente Schagen. Omvang Het aantal opdrachten, vanaf schaal 10 Cao gemeenten, is ongeveer 20 op jaarbasis, hieraan kunnen geen rechten worden ontleend. Ook kunnen gedurende de looptijd nieuwe organisaties aan dit Dynamisch Aankoopsysteem worden toegevoegd. Zij behouden zich het recht voor om jaarlijks, zonder opgaaf van redenen, het DAS te kunnen beëindigen. The Government requires the procurement of a Modernized Airborne Radio Control Head (MARCH) / Control Head Unit (CHU) solution to provide form, fit, function, and interface (F3I) cockpit radio control for the Air-to-Ground Networking Radio (AGNR) System and to replace the obsolete C-12601 Control Indicator (CI) within the AN/ARC-231A Radio Set across Army tactical rotorcraft (UH-60M/V Black Hawk, CH-47F Chinook, AH-64D/E Apache), designated fixed-wing aircraft, and unmanned aircraft systems (UAS). This effort will procure commercial-derivative Communication Management Units (CMUs), Mercury Systems ACM-9000 series hardware, specifically ACM-9544 CHUs and ACM-9443J CIs. The scope also encompasses airworthiness certification data and artifacts, proprietary operating system and runtime software licenses, and modernized MARCH engineering design, systems integration, and qualification testing services. This acquisition is being conducted on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 and RFO 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii), which authorizes contracting other than full and open competition when there is only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Mercury Systems, Inc. is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the sole owner of the proprietary hardware manufacturing data packages, circuit schematics, FPGA register configurations, and safety-critical software source code for the qualified ACM-9544 and ACM-9443J units. The Government does not possess licensing rights to this technical data, and any alternative vendor would require an estimated 18 to 30 months to redesign, environmentally qualify, and airworthiness certify a replacement system. title: Norway – Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses) – GC-HRMS
description: The objective of the procurement is to enter into a contract for the procurement of a GC-HRMS system that can perform quantitative analysis on ultra low levels of environmental toxins in complex matrixes. The Norwegian Institute of Marine Research (HI) is one of Europe's largest marine research institutes and our laboratories are the National Reference Laboratory (NRL) for several parameters within the marine area. We would now like to expand our instrument fleet with a GC-HRMS system that can perform quantitative analysis on ultra low levels of environmental toxins in complex matrixes. The system shall provide the sensitivity, selectivity, mass resolution and quantitative performance required for routine monitoring, research, method development and activities at a national reference laboratory. Primary areas of use include: · PCDD/F · Dioxin-like PCB (dl-PCB) · Other halogenated POPs and dioxin-like compounds The main matrixes will include: · Marine biota and seafood · Feeding ingredients and fish feed. · Biological/human tissue · Sediment and water With this variation in potentially relevant applications, user friendliness and minimal downtime are very important. In addition to the primary use for quantitative analyses of dioxins and dioxin-like compounds, the system shall support method development and broader GC-HRMS applications, including target orientated quantitative analysis and screening of volatile and semi-volatile organic contaminants. Further applications can include bronchosmated flame retardants, chlorinated paraffin, pesticides, PAH, plastic-assisted chemicals, PFAS related compounds that can be analysed with GC and any other future contaminants. As a part of the evaluation, tenderers shall analyse a set of samples delivered by HI in order to demonstrate the performance of the offered GC-HRMS system for PCDD/F, dioxin-like and non-dioxin-like PCBs, PBDE and HRMS screening. Tenderers shall submit a technical report describing the analytical method, instrument configuration, procedures for data acquisition and data processing, quality control as well as analytical results. See Annex 3a for further details. See annex 3 - requirement specifications for further details on the delivery.

title: Facet Coater
description: For over two decades, the Canadian Photonics Fabrication Centre (CPFC) at the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) has operated as a mission-critical facility supporting Canada’s photonics and semiconductor innovation ecosystem. The CPFC provides advanced fabrication and metrology services for both internal research programs and external clients, enabling the development and production of cutting-edge photonic devices used in telecommunications, sensing, and quantum technologies. Photonic devices are critical pieces of hardware for high-performance computing in various innovative fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), data centres, automotive LiDARs (Light Detection and Ranging), biomedical, aerospace; security, and quantum industry/applications. The global market for compound semiconductor foundry services is growing rapidly, presenting niche opportunities and challenges for Canada. Limited access to compound semiconductor foundry services poses several challenges to develop, successfully introduce, and supply new products in an increasingly competitive marketplace. Photonic devices fabricated on InP wafers must undergo several “back-end” steps before dicing and packaging, adding time and cost if the assembled parts are then found to be defective. This project will establish the capability at CPFC to deliver known good die (KGD) to clients, to reduce time and cost for new product introduction (NPI). To provide KGD, a new clean room (ISO 6) will be constructed (retrofit of a current facility) to house numerous automated tools, such as Dual Ion Beam Sputter Deposition (DIBS) Laser Facet Coating Systems. This project will address an immediate client need for timely introduction of new products into a competitive marketplace.

description: Amendment 1 - Answers to timely submitted questions are attached. NEW SUBMISSION DATE - Monday, November 16, 2026 - 4:00PM ET. ______________________________________________________________ The Department of War (DOW) Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation (CAPE) supports the Office of the Secretary of War (OSW). The Director of CAPE is the principal staff assistant to the Secretary of War for Cost Assessment & Program Evaluation. In fulfilling this role, the Director of CAPE provides independent, non-advocate, and data-driven analytical evaluations directly to the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War regarding defense program investments, major force structure posture, and strategic resourcing trade-offs. The Director�s principal responsibilities include: Analyze and evaluate plans, programs, and budgets in relation to U.S. defense objectives, projected threats, allied contributions, estimated costs, and resource constraints. Review, analyze, and evaluate programs, including classified programs, for executing approved policies. Provide leadership in developing and promoting improved analytical tools and methods for analyzing national security planning and the allocation of resources. Ensure that the costs of DoW programs, including classified programs, are presented accurately and completely. Assess effects of DoW spending on the U.S. economy and evaluate alternative policies to ensure that DoW programs can be implemented efficiently. Currently, CAPE�s campaign- and mission-level Modeling and Simulation (M&S) relies on heavy, time-intensive physics engines (e.g., AFSIM) that execute discrete, bespoke combat runs. While highly detailed, these simulation approaches are too slow, computationally expensive, and inflexible to support executive-level sensitivity sweeps across multi-dimensional threat environments and Department warfighting capabilities. CAPE�s current environment leverages HPC resources that provide 1.5 terabytes (TB) of usable memory and 2,000 Central Processing Unit (CPU) cores with no wall clock time restraints. On average, individual simulation execution via AFSIM requires 1 hour of real time to complete and 20 gigabytes (GB) of accessible RAM. This constraint, coupled with sharp disparities in compute architecture, hardware availability, and security accreditation across existing CAPE enclaves restrict analysts to limited, manual workflows while preventing the execution of high-throughput, compute-intensive campaign analytics. CAPE is seeking innovative solutions to establish a next-generation modeling architecture, replacing its legacy M&S infrastructure. To dramatically compress the cycle time between defense budget queries and statistically defensible warfighting insights, the target environment must integrate three interdependent functional layers: (1) A high-performance simulation execution layer to execute large numbers of model (e.g., AFSIM) runs to span the parameter space. Runs in this layer are computationally intensive and resource demanding but will be executed infrequently and systematically using advanced Design of Experiments techniques. (2) A machine-learned surrogate emulation layer to train ultra-fast emulator models from simulation results and detect out-of-sample queries. While the government plans to develop and calibrate these surrogate emulators and analytical models in-house, the commercial solution must provide the extensible data staging, pipeline integration, and execution framework to ingest batch simulation results and host these government-developed models. (3) An intuitive self-service quantitative analysis layer housing pre-built methods for sensitivity analysis, marginal gain estimates, etc., and tools for custom analysis (e.g., tradespace decisions between range, speed, and lethality of weapon systems) and visualization. The solution must support both current operational needs and have flexibility to accommodate future growth in data volume, model complexity, user demand, and computational intensity. This next generation environment will establish an open, scalable, and unified computational backbone designed to modernize Department decision support. The scope of this effort includes the following core technical and performance requirements. A high-performance compute environment sized to meet demanding modeling, simulation, and analytic workloads. Proposed solution architectures should span options to allow for parameter evaluation in the simulation layer on the order of 1,200 individual simulations (i.e., light case - isolated missions only) to be executed within 10 hours real-time, up to 150,000 individual simulations (i.e., heavy case � full joint campaign) to be executed within 2 weeks real-time. Of note, current CAPE architecture would require 1 year of simulation execution runtime for the heavy case. Secure, efficient, data and software movement both into and out of the environment, as well as the ability to interface with external networks to enable transfer of data in accordance with applicable security and access controls. The environment must support network throughput of 100 Mbps - 1 Gbps. The solution must also support connectivity over HTTPS to designated external OSW and mission-relevant data sources, including OSW CAPE-furnished databases and other authorized repositories (e.g., War Data Platform), as applicable. Ability to accommodate evolving development ecosystems and diverse sets of software including M&S tools and analytic technologies. This includes modern software (e.g., Python, R, Java, etc.), scalable data platforms, scalable parallelizable processes (e.g., containers), optimization tools (e.g., GAMS), artificial intelligence capabilities (e.g., large language models), and neural network development (e.g., PyTorch), provided they can be incorporated in a secure and maintainable manner. The solution must enable efficient onboarding, integration, and removal of models and software as mission needs evolve. The Government will retain full operational tenant administration, maintaining exclusive control over user access provisioning, role-based security permissions, data ingestion, proprietary model uploads, container orchestration, and analytical query execution. The Commercial provider will be responsible for turnkey, managed platform and infrastructure IT operations, including hardware availability, operating system patching, network performance, automated system backups, and baseline cybersecurity hardening, ensuring government analysts and technical leads are fully insulated from day-to-day hardware maintenance and IT administration.

title: Germany – General management consultancy services – 10035189-Advice on implementation of AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol and technical inputs to related reforms; facilitation and development of partnerships with the private sector on digital trade
description: The project "Pan-African e-Commerce Initiative 3 - Boosting African Digital Trade" (PeCI 3) is a regional technical cooperation project implemented by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) in the context of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The project aims to strengthen an enabling environment for cross-border digital trade in Africa, with a particular focus on micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), including women-led businesses. PeCI 3 contributes to the BMZ"s core area "Sustainable Economic Development, Training and Employment" and supports it"s digital policy and Africa Strategy through the promotion of inclusive digital trade ecosystems, and public-private cooperation. The project builds on the achievements and partnerships established under the previous phases (PeCI 1 and PeCI 2). Earlier phases supported MSMEs in adopting e-commerce solutions and digital sales channels, strengthened intermediary organisations providing training and advisory services, facilitated public-private exchange on digital trade issues and contributed to regional approaches related to e-commerce, digital payments, consumer protection and electronic transactions. The project also strengthened cooperation with the East African Community (EAC), the Smart Africa Alliance (SAA) and the AfCFTA Secretariat. PeCI 3 supports implementation of the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol (DTP), adopted by the African Union in 2024, by strengthening structures, processes and cooperation mechanisms required for cross-border digital trade. The project addresses barriers affecting MSME participation in digital trade, including fragmented regulatory frameworks, limited interoperability of digital payment systems, logistics and last-mile delivery challenges, gaps in online consumer protection and limited coordination between public and private actors. Particular attention is given to barriers affecting women"s participation in digital trade ecosystems. The project operates at pan-African, regional and national levels and combines technical advisory services, stakeholder consultations, public-private dialogue formats and capacity development measures. Activities include support for implementation of selected DTP chapters, facilitation of cross-border exchange on best practices, development of cooperation models between private-sector actors and intermediary organisations, and support for gender-sensitive approaches to digital entrepreneurship and MSME support services. Environmental sustainability is integrated as a cross-cutting topic, including approaches related to sustainable packaging and resource-efficient logistics. The project is implemented in cooperation with public, private and regional stakeholders in selected AfCFTA countries, particularly Ghana and Kenya, as well as with the EAC. Lead executing agencies are the Ministry of Finance in Ghana, the Ministry of Investments, Trade and Industry (MITI) in Kenya and the EAC Secretariat. Additional partners include the AfCFTA Secretariat, the Smart Africa Secretariat, chambers of commerce, business and e-commerce associations, payment service providers, logistics companies, innovation hubs and women"s business networks. PeCI 3 further aims to strengthen cooperation between African, German and European private-sector actors to promote cross-border digital trade and MSME participation. The project cooperates with business associations, e-commerce platforms, logistics and payment providers, chambers of commerce and innovation actors, including bevh, AHKs and African e-commerce associations. Cooperation with UNCTAD, ITC and initiatives supported by the European Union and the World Bank further strengthens synergies and regional outreach. The project is scheduled to run until June 2028.

title: Belgium – Washing and dry-cleaning services – Raamovereenkomst voor huur en onderhoud van plat linnen en beroepskledij
description: Deze opdracht wordt uitgeschreven door vzw Algemeen Ziekenhuis Klina, Augustijnslei 100, 2930 Brasschaat, KBO nr. 0434.302.850, hierna aangeduid als de aanbestedende overheid en AZ Klina. Elke onderneming die een offerte indient, wordt aangeduid als inschrijver. De inschrijver aan wie de overheidsopdracht wordt gegund, wordt na gunning aangeduid als de leverancier. Voor meer informatie over AZ Klina kan de website worden geraadpleegd: https://www.azklina.be. Deze opdracht betreft een raamovereenkomst voor het huren, wassen, drogen, herstellen en/of vervangen en het transport van linnen, dekbedden en beroepskledij voor AZ Klina. Daarnaast omvat de opdracht het ter beschikking stellen en het onderhouden van logistieke hulpmiddelen, zoals rolcontainers, kapstokhouders en plastic zakken, die noodzakelijk zijn voor een efficiënte inzameling, verwerking en distributie van het textiel. De opdracht wordt uitgevoerd voor een initiële periode van 48 maanden en kan éénmalig stilzwijgend worden verlengd met een bijkomende periode van 48 maanden waardoor de totale looptijd maximaal acht jaar bedraagt. De op en afhaalactiviteiten zijn gespreid over de volgende hoofdlocaties van AZ Klina:  Campus Klina;  Campus De Mick;  Campus Coda. Daarnaast is éénmaal per week een afhaling en levering voorzien op Campus Klina – Versailles. De opdracht omvat de huur en/of het onderhoud van de volgende productgroepen:  badlinnen;  bedlinnen;  keuken en restauratielinnen;  patiëntenkledij (zoals infuushemden, patiëntenhemden, bezoekersschorten, …);  arbeidskledij. De verdeling van de beroepskledij binnen AZ Klina gebeurt grotendeels via geautomatiseerde kledijuitgifte en innamesystemen. De opdrachtnemer dient zijn dienstverlening hier naadloos op af te stemmen. De raamovereenkomst gaat in zes maanden na de datum vermeld in de sluitingsbrief. De indicatieve opstartdatum van de dienstverlening is voorzien op februari 2027, rekening houdend met de noodzakelijke overgangsperiode tussen de huidige en de nieuwe dienstverlener. Het doel van deze opdracht is het aanstellen van een betrouwbare en deskundige partner die instaat voor een kwalitatieve, efficiënte en duurzame uitvoering van de bovenvermelde diensten, met een optimale prijs kwaliteitsverhouding. Daarbij wordt geen exclusiviteit gegarandeerd. Van de opdrachtnemer wordt tevens verwacht dat deze proactief meedenkt en ondersteunt bij de optimalisatie van producten, processen en dienstverlening, in functie van de noden en werking van AZ Klina

title: Finland – Translation services – Valtioneuvoston ja oikeuskanslerinviraston monikielisiä käännöspalveluita koskeva puitejärjestely 2027-2029 (2030/2031)
description: Valtioneuvoston kanslia (VNK) vastaa valtioneuvoston ja sen ministeriöiden yhteisistä hallinto- ja palvelutehtävistä. Valtioneuvoston kanslia huolehtii kaikkien ministeriöiden käännös- ja kielipalveluista sekä kansalliskielille että muille kielille. Lisäksi VNK huolehtii osin oikeuskanslerinviraston tarvitsemista käännös- ja kielipalveluista. Hankinnan kohteena on valtioneuvoston ja sen ministeriöiden monikielisiä käännöspalveluita koskevat puitejärjestelyt, jotka täydentävät valtioneuvoston ruotsin ja englannin kielten käännöspalveluita koskevia puitejärjestelyjä (VN/33137/2023). Lisäksi hankinnan kohteena ovat oikeuskanslerinviraston tarvitsemat käännöspalvelut (pois lukien oikeuskanslerinviraston ruotsin käännöspalvelut). Käännökset voivat koskea mitä tahansa ministeriöiden toimialoihin kuuluvaa asiaa, ks. valtioneuvoston ohjesääntö 262/2003, § 10–24, http://www.finlex.fi/fi/laki/ajantasa/2003/20030262. Lisätietoa ministeriöiden toimialoista on saatavilla myös ministeriöiden www-sivustoilla, ks. https://valtioneuvosto.fi/ministeriot. Oikeuskansleri valvoo hallituksen ja ministeriöiden sekä tasavallan presidentin virkatoimien lainmukaisuutta. Hän valvoo myös, että tuomioistuimet, viranomaiset ja virkamiehet sekä muut julkista tehtävää hoitavat noudattavat lakia ja täyttävät velvollisuutensa. Lisäksi oikeuskanslerilla on asianajajien valvontaan liittyviä tehtäviä. Oikeuskansleri toimii valtioneuvoston yhteydessä. Lisätietoa oikeuskanslerin tehtävistä ja oikeuskanslerinvirastosta: https://www.okv.fi/fi/. Oikeuskanslerinviraston käännöstarpeet koskevat osa-aluetta 2 ja erityisesti englannin käännöksiä. Satunnaisesti on tarvetta myös muiden kielten käännöksille pois lukien ruotsinkieliset käännökset. Hankinta on jaettu kahteen osa-alueeseen: Osa-alue 1 KKV- ja TES-käännökset (suomi-ruotsi) • ministereiden vastauksia kansanedustajien tekemiin kirjallisiin kysymyksiin (KKV) • työehtosopimuksia (TES) • valitaan kaksi (2) toimittajaa Osa-alue 2 Muut käännökset, useita kielipareja • raportteja ja selvityksiä ja niiden tiivistelmiä • verkkosivutekstejä • PowerPoint-esityksiä • valitaan kolme (3) toimittajaa Hankittavan palvelun kuvaus on esitetty tarjouspyynnön liitteessä 1 Palvelukuvaus. Tarjoaja voi tarjota joko yhteen tai molempiin osa-alueisiin. Hankinnan perusteella perustetaan molemmille osa-alueille useamman toimittajan puitejärjestelyt. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvo on molemmat osa-alueet yhteenlaskettuna noin 475 000 euroa vuodessa ja valittavien toimittajien kanssa tehdään kahden vuoden määräaikaiset puitesopimukset, joissa varataan mahdollisuus käyttää kaksi optiovuotta (1+1). Sopimuskausi alkaa arviolta 1.2.2027.

title: Directors and Officers insurance (D&O insurance) for EIFO - primary layer
description: Introduction to EIFO: EIFO was established as an independent public enterprise pursuant to Act No. 871 of 21 June 2022 on Denmark’s Export and Investment Fund (the “EIFO Act”). EIFO serves as Denmark’s official export credit agency (ECA) and national promotional bank (NPB). EIFO provides financing and risk capital with the aim of promoting growth and innovation in Danish businesses, supporting their export and internationalisation activities, and contributing to a sustainable and green transition. As a state-owned financial institution with a global perspective and an AAA credit rating, EIFO offers a range of financial solutions to Danish companies and their international customers and partners. EIFO also invests directly in companies and in funds, including funds focused on innovation and technology. EIFO complements the private market by providing financing and risk capital in areas where private market participants are generally unable or unwilling to undertake the relevant activity due to its nature, scale or associated risk. In this capacity, EIFO supports Danish companies at different stages of development, ranging from start-ups and SMEs with growth ambitions to established export companies seeking financing for international expansion and entry into new markets. In cooperation with Danish and international banks, financial institutions, leasing companies and investors, EIFO provides, among other things, loans, guarantees and various forms of equity financing to Danish companies across all stages of their development. For further information about EIFO, please see the following website: https://eifo.dk/ Tender: This tender concerns a contract for EIFO’ Directors and Officers insurance (D&O insurance) covering the primary layer. Please refer to the tender material for information about capacity (limits and retention), risk assessment, and the time and activity plan. The information will not be shared publicly but can be obtained directly from the contact persons. Questions are to be addressed to the contact person in writing as soon as possible and no later than November 10, 2026. title: Tampa Harbor Improvements Industry Day
description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an industry day event on 18 November 2026 at 9:00AM EST. All interested Offerors are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view registration information and details below. The presentation slides and list of attendees will be made available and posted to the subject special notice on SAM.gov after the conclusion of the event. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District will be holding an Industry Day event to gauge the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of various members of the Construction Community, to include Small Businesses, and to also provide information and obtain feedback from interested Offerors prior to issuance of the official solicitation. This requirement is for fiscal year (FY) 2028 award. NAICS Code 237990: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Standard: $37 million Magnitude of Construction: $100 - $500 million Project Title: Tampa Harbor Improvements Industry Day. Purpose: The purpose of this scheduled Industry Day is to provide the latest information regarding the future advertisement and award of Contract 1 for the Tampa Harbor Deepening Project. The scheduled event will include a detailed presentation by the Jacksonville District US Army Corps of Engineers, Tampa Harbor Project Delivery Team (PDT) followed by open Q&A and 1-1 meeting opportunities with contracts to ask more in-depth questions and get feedback as the design and permitting moves forward. Project Description: The project includes construction dredging to deepen and widen specified areas within the federal navigation channel of Tampa Harbor. The project is planned for six (6) contracts over an estimated 8�10-year period. The Scope of Work for this Industry Day will be focused on Contract 1. Contract 1 work includes deepening of Cut-C (HB), Port Sutton Channel, Port Sutton Turning Basin, East Bay Channel and Cut-D (HB) to a depth of 49 feet MLLW, deepening the Port Sutton Terminal Channel to a depth of 44 feet MLLW, and deepening the East Bay Channel Extensions 1 and 2 to a depth of 41 feet MLLW. The Contract 1 work also includes widening of Port Sutton Channel, Port Sutton Turning Basin, and East Bay Channel. All areas of deepening and widening will incorporate +1 foot of allowable overdepth. All dredged material from the project will be disposed of in the East Bay Placement Area, DMMA 2-D and DMMA 3-D. Estimated quantities to be dredged are roughly 4.4 million cubic yards. Link to the Tampa Harbor Improvements USACE website: https://www.saj.usace.army.mil/Tampa-Harbor/-30-/ Requests for Information: Industry is asked to consider the following questions and provide input at the Industry Day: 1. Company/Contractor name, address, point of contact, phone number and e-mail address. 2. Does the Contractor plan to submit a proposal for this contract? 3. Describe the proposed construction methods and sequencing and equipment needed to complete the project. At a minimum, address pre-dredging, side-casting of pre-dredging material, and placement into the East Bay Placement Area including constructing the containment perimeter and filling within the area. The contract will include geologic data of the dredge and placement areas as well as the geotechnical requirements for materials considered suitable for constructing the containment perimeter. The contractor will propose the dredging sequence to accomplish constructing the containment perimeter that meets required geotechnical specifications. Describe the factors considered in determining the dredging sequence, such as the material type, proposed equipment, proximity to the placement area, etc.? 4. Describe any constructability, stability, safety concerns with East Bay Placement Area. Describe additional equipment or methods required to place infill above water and/or above the proposed crest of the containment perimeter. Describe any concerns for drainage of the placement area. 5. Describe how filling the East Bay Placement Area will not result in material migrating out of the placement area and into the federal channel. At a minimum, address how existing soft material at the placement area will be contained when disturbed. 6. Will the proposed East Bay Placement Area construction methods require equipment to be located within the federal channel for extended periods of time acting as obstructions for vessel traffic, or obstruct Port Tampa Bay Berth 150? 7. For East Bay Placement Area, describe any temporal facilities, staging and laydown areas, and utilities that would be required or preferred in adjacent upland areas. 8. Dredging and placement of material will be conducted in a manner to minimize turbidity. Describe the turbidity control measures, such as turbidity curtains, that would be incorporated into the proposed construction methodology. If hydraulic placement of infill is proposed for the East Bay Placement Area, describe how affluent will be managed. 9. Based on prior dredging construction experience either in Tampa Bay or other locations in Florida, what are some of the challenges USACE could streamline to improve contract execution? 10. Describe any concerns with execution of the environmental species monitoring and reporting. Event Date: Wednesday, 18 November 2026 at 9:00 AM EST. Event Location: Port of Tampa � Cruise Terminal 6 1331 McKay Street Tampa, Florida 33602 *Parking available onsite For more information, please see the Industry Day Agenda copy under the Attachments. title: Tampa Harbor Improvements Industry Day
description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation.
