The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District will be holding an Industry Day event to gauge the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of various members of the Construction Community, to include Small Businesses, and to also provide information and obtain feedback from interested Offerors prior to issuance of the official solicitation. This requirement is for fiscal year (FY) 2028 award. NAICS Code 237990: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Standard: $37 million Magnitude of Construction: $100 - $500 million Project Title: Tampa Harbor Improvements Industry Day. Purpose: The purpose of this scheduled Industry Day is to provide the latest information regarding the future advertisement and award of Contract 1 for the Tampa Harbor Deepening Project. The scheduled event will include a detailed presentation by the Jacksonville District US Army Corps of Engineers, Tampa Harbor Project Delivery Team (PDT) followed by open Q&A and 1-1 meeting opportunities with contracts to ask more in-depth questions and get feedback as the design and permitting moves forward. Project Description: The project includes construction dredging to deepen and widen specified areas within the federal navigation channel of Tampa Harbor. The project is planned for six (6) contracts over an estimated 8�10-year period. The Scope of Work for this Industry Day will be focused on Contract 1. Contract 1 work includes deepening of Cut-C (HB), Port Sutton Channel, Port Sutton Turning Basin, East Bay Channel and Cut-D (HB) to a depth of 49 feet MLLW, deepening the Port Sutton Terminal Channel to a depth of 44 feet MLLW, and deepening the East Bay Channel Extensions 1 and 2 to a depth of 41 feet MLLW. The Contract 1 work also includes widening of Port Sutton Channel, Port Sutton Turning Basin, and East Bay Channel. All areas of deepening and widening will incorporate +1 foot of allowable overdepth. All dredged material from the project will be disposed of in the East Bay Placement Area, DMMA 2-D and DMMA 3-D. Estimated quantities to be dredged are roughly 4.4 million cubic yards. Link to the Tampa Harbor Improvements USACE website: https://www.saj.usace.army.mil/Tampa-Harbor/-30-/ Requests for Information: Industry is asked to consider the following questions and provide input at the Industry Day: 1. Company/Contractor name, address, point of contact, phone number and e-mail address. 2. Does the Contractor plan to submit a proposal for this contract? 3. Describe the proposed construction methods and sequencing and equipment needed to complete the project. At a minimum, address pre-dredging, side-casting of pre-dredging material, and placement into the East Bay Placement Area including constructing the containment perimeter and filling within the area. The contract will include geologic data of the dredge and placement areas as well as the geotechnical requirements for materials considered suitable for constructing the containment perimeter. The contractor will propose the dredging sequence to accomplish constructing the containment perimeter that meets required geotechnical specifications. Describe the factors considered in determining the dredging sequence, such as the material type, proposed equipment, proximity to the placement area, etc.? 4. Describe any constructability, stability, safety concerns with East Bay Placement Area. Describe additional equipment or methods required to place infill above water and/or above the proposed crest of the containment perimeter. Describe any concerns for drainage of the placement area. 5. Describe how filling the East Bay Placement Area will not result in material migrating out of the placement area and into the federal channel. At a minimum, address how existing soft material at the placement area will be contained when disturbed. 6. Will the proposed East Bay Placement Area construction methods require equipment to be located within the federal channel for extended periods of time acting as obstructions for vessel traffic, or obstruct Port Tampa Bay Berth 150? 7. For East Bay Placement Area, describe any temporal facilities, staging and laydown areas, and utilities that would be required or preferred in adjacent upland areas. 8. Dredging and placement of material will be conducted in a manner to minimize turbidity. Describe the turbidity control measures, such as turbidity curtains, that would be incorporated into the proposed construction methodology. If hydraulic placement of infill is proposed for the East Bay Placement Area, describe how affluent will be managed. 9. Based on prior dredging construction experience either in Tampa Bay or other locations in Florida, what are some of the challenges USACE could streamline to improve contract execution? 10. title: Coburn Gore LPOE Art in Architecture Project
description: Document Added & Updated: 0332CG-AIA- Coburn Gore AIA Questions & Answers V3 Dated 07 October 2026 The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents or Permanent Workers of the United States) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal buildings nationwide. GSA announces an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the new construction of the Coburn Gore Land Port of Entry (LPOE) in Coburn, Maine. The new facility will strengthen supply chains, improve operational capabilities and facility infrastructure, spur economic growth, and bolster the country�s security. The project will provide a fully operational LPOE that coordinates with the tra?c ?ow and operations of the Canadian port of entry at Saint-Augustin-de-Woburn Quebec, Port of Entry. The project will provide a new port that allows Customs and Border Protection to more efficiently carry out its agency mission, their operations and interactions with the public. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $275,000 to $400,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by the SAM Contract Opportunity�s Response Date. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). Instructions on how to submit application materials and join the Registry are available on the following Web site: https://www.gsa.gov/real-estate/design-and-construction/art-in-architecturefine-arts/art-in-architecture-program/art-in-architecture-national-artist-registry All artists who wish to be considered as candidates for a commission at the LPOE in Coburn Gore, ME must have their application materials submitted and received by GSA by 12:00 PM Eastern Time on 18 November 2026. Artists� submissions received after the deadline will not be considered for this project but will be eligible for consideration on future GSA commissions alongside the other artists on the Registry. Artists already on the Registry need not resubmit but may elect to update their information prior to the deadline. GSA evaluates artists based on the following criteria: the media, materials, content and style of the artist�s past work, along with the artist�s past performance and experience with commissions or projects similar to the one described in this synopsis. Shortlisted artists will be contacted and asked to submit additional information, including a statement that the artist can perform the work associated with the GSA commission within the identified budget. GSA will count the combined weight of all the selection criteria as significantly more important than price. At minimum, the scope of services for this commission will require collaboration with the lead designer selected for the land port of entry project; travel to the project site; development and presentation of preliminary and final concepts; fabrication of the artwork; participation in meetings and conservation reviews as necessary; delivery and installation of the artwork; professional documentation of, and detailed maintenance planning for the artwork at the project site. For informational purposes: Artists selected for the contract award must be Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of award. Instructions for creating an account and activating registration in SAM may be found at www.sam.gov. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to renew the registration in SAM on an annual basis for the duration of the project. In accordance with Executive Order (EO) 13934, agencies should prioritize the commission of works of art that portray historically significant Americans or events of American historical significance or illustrate the ideals upon which our Nation was founded. Inquiries concerning the project should be directed to the following email address: Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov and reference the synopsis number in the subject line. No questions will be answered after 07 October 2026 12:00pm EST.

title: Senior Project Management services for IT development for the State Agency for Reconstruction and Infrastructure Development of Ukraine
description: Description EU4Reconstruction. The European Union (EU), together with Denmark, Germany, France and Lithuania, launched EU4Reconstruction, a €37 million Team Europe Initiative (TEI) that unites the strength, experience and solidarity of the EU to support Ukraine’s ongoing recovery and reconstruction. The initiative aims to strengthen governance, improve public investment management, and enhance coordination across levels of government, with a strong emphasis on EU values. The TEl is divided in two parallel streams; one stream is composed of GIZ (Lead Organisation) and Expertise France (Partner Organisation) and the other gathers the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark (Lead Organisation) and Central Project Management Agency (Partner Organisation). EU4Reconstruction will reinforce the leadership of the Ministry for Restoration, Infrastructure and Transport of Ukraine, strengthen the State Agency for Reconstruction and Development of Infrastructure (SARDI or Agency), empower local governments to manage reconstruction professionally and sustainably, and support civil society and independent media to play an active role in oversight, ensuring public trust and reducing corruption risks. Purpose The purpose of this assignment is to strengthen SARDI’s institutional capacity to manage its digital transformation initiatives through expert guidance, knowledge transfer and mentoring. Objective The specific objectives of the assignment are to: ● provide expert support and methodological guidance and supporting SARDI in planning and overseeing the development and implementation of digital systems, in line with the Agency’s objectives and needs; ● facilitate coordination between SARDI, EU4Reconstruction, IT contractors and technical experts engaged by EU4Reconstruction, while ensuring that SARDI retains ownership of project processes and key decisions; ● strengthen the skills and knowledge of SARDI staff through mentoring, knowledge transfer and practical guidance on IT project management, business requirements, digital solution implementation and contractor coordination. Scope of work In close coordination with EU4Reconstruction Stream 2 and SARDI’s leadership (CDTO and relevant Deputy Heads), the Senior Project Manager shall provide IT project management expertise, methodological guidance and capacity-building support to strengthen SARDI’s ability to lead and manage its digital transformation activities. The services shall cover, inter alia, the project performance management and monitoring IT system, the asset management IT system, the corporate web portal, the tender documentation development and management IT system, and other systems supported by EU4Reconstruction Stream 2 (together, the “Digital Transformation Activities” or “DTA”). Timing and Budget The intended commencement date is the date of signature of the contract with the Consultant and the period of implementation of the contract will be 20 months, with a tentative start in November 2026. The assignment includes up to 420 working days per full term of the Contract. The expert is expected to work in Kyiv and come to the premises of the Agency upon short notice. The maximum budget available for this assignment is up to 605,435.00 DKK (EUR 81,000.00), inclusive of all applicable expenses and taxes. Deadline for application : 19-November-2026 at 14:00 Danish time Interested Consultants can request to get the instructions prepared for applicants by e-mail to the Contact person stated below Contact point EU4Reconstruction Contact person Dmytro Petrenko Contact e-mail dmypet@um.dk Criteria for selection A minimum of three and a maximum of five applicants with references best suited for the assignment will be invited to submit a tender.

title: Sources Sought Notice: United States Naval Academy Infoblox Trinzic Equipment
description: Subject to FAR Clause 52.215-3, entitled "Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes," this announcement constitutes a Sources Sought for information and planning purposes for qualified and experienced sources to provide upgrade equipment for the United States Naval Academy (USNA) Infoblox DNS, DHCP, and IP Address Management (DDI) Grid. This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. It is not to be construed in any way as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response. BACKGROUND: The United States Naval Academy (USNA) Information Technology Services Division (ITSD) is responsible for developing, managing and integrating information systems and providing information technology products, services and capabilities for approximately 7,000 midshipmen, faculty and staff across the academy�s 630-acre campus and for the approximately 300 midshipmen candidates, faculty and staff at the Naval Academy Preparatory School (NAPS) located in Newport R.I. The proposed acquisition is to purchase equipment required to upgrade the existing, in-place USNA Infoblox DNS, DHCP, and IP Address Management (DDI) Grid, which provides core network naming and addressing services across USNA. The equipment purchased will replace older, like appliances that are swiftly approaching end of life and end of support by the manufacturer. The procurement will be a direct, one-for-one replacement of the 15 existing Infoblox Grid appliances; to include 10 Infoblox Trinzic X6 906 appliances, 4 Infoblox Trinzic X6 1506 appliances, and 1 Infoblox Trinzic X6 1606 appliance, along with the associated NIOS software subscriptions, Premium Maintenance-Enterprise support, power supplies, and peripheral devices required to accomplish life cycle replacement. A Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Delivery / Purchase Order under NAICS Code 423430 is anticipated. NAICS CODE: The NAICS Code for this requirement is 423430, Computer and Computer Peripheral Equipment and Software Merchant Wholesalers, and the Small Business Size Standard is 250 (# of employees). RFI SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested parties shall submit responses to this Sources Sought Notice for consideration and shall include the following information (Please reference N0018927QL222 in your response) 1. Company name, address, Point of Contact name, phone number, and email address. 2. Contractor and Government Entity (CAGE) Code and DUNS Number. 3. Statement as to whether business is actively registered in the System for Award Management 4. Size of business- Large Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged, 8(a), HUBZONE, Woman-Owned and/or Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business under the applicable NAICS. 5. Indicate if your company can be a prime contractor for this effort or, if not, whether your company can be a subcontractor. If subcontractors are to be used, provide the anticipated percentage of effort to be subcontracted and if a small or large businesses will be used. 6. If the items/services can be obtained from an existing Government contract vehicle, to include, but not limited to, GSA, NASA SEWP, SeaPort-NxG, DoW ESI. Please provide the applicable contract number if available from a Government contract vehicle. 7.Capability statement displaying the offerors ability to provide the minimum requirements to include past performance information. If past performance information is provided, please include only relevant past performance on the same/similar work within the last 5 years. Please also include in past performance information the contract numbers, dollar value, and period of performance for each contract referenced in the response to this sources sought. This announcement is NOT a contract, request for proposal, a promise to contract, or a commitment of any kind on the part of the U.S. Government. Standard company brochures will not be reviewed. Submissions are not to exceed five (5) typewritten pages in no less than 12 font. All technical questions and inquiries may be submitted within the response. The Government is determining the acquisition strategy for this potential acquisition. Note that if there is sufficient demonstrated interest and capability among small businesses, a key factor in determining if an acquisition will be a small business set-aside is that two or more potential small business prime contractors must be capable of performing at least 50% of the effort, as defined in FAR clause 52.219-14. title: Market Survey: Manufacturing and Delivery of modular, transportable building units or shipping containers to Key West, Florida.
description: 1. Purpose The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is conducting a market survey to identify qualified, capable industry sources for the manufacturing and delivery of modular, transportable building units or shipping containers to Key West, Florida. This announcement serves to assess vendor capability, determine commercial availability, and gather industry feedback on alternative project delivery and contracting strategies. The findings will assist the FAA in developing its acquisition strategy and procurement planning in accordance with FAA AMS � 3.2.1.2.1. 2. General Project Description & Scope of Work The baseline requirement comprises an estimated ten (10) structural units (shipping containers or modular building units) meeting the following preliminary specifications: Dimensions & Configuration: Assembled footprint of approximately 30 ft (W) � 48 ft (L), with a minimum interior clear ceiling height of 8 ft. Components must be engineered for highway transit, crane rigging/lifting, and rapid on-site assembly. Structural Integrity: Robust structural construction designed to withstand repeated transport, rigging, crane operations, and installation at the project site. Thermal Envelope: Fully insulated exterior walls and roof system achieving an approximate thermal resistance rating of R-28. Identification & Sequencing: Clear, weather-resistant exterior markings to facilitate accurate component identification, planned erection sequencing, and future disassembly/relocation. Modularization & Mobility: 100% modular and fully relocatable. The baseline 10-module configuration was developed to reduce road-permitting constraints; however, the FAA invites alternative modularization concepts (fewer or more modules) if they demonstrate clear efficiencies in freight transit, site assembly, or future relocation. Commercial modular alternatives or standard ISO shipping containers are encouraged. Regulatory Compliance: Full compliance with the Buy American Act (BAA). All proposed equipment, assemblies, and primary components must satisfy domestic manufacturing and sourcing criteria. Place of Delivery: Key West, Florida. Delivery Schedule: Target Delivery Date: February 1, 2027 Mandatory Delivery Completion: February 28, 2027 (dates remain subject to negotiation) 3. Submission of Capability Statements Interested vendors are requested to provide a preliminary Capability Statement addressing the following areas: Technical Capability: Confirmation of ability to satisfy or exceed the structural, dimensional, and thermal requirements, including technical overviews of any proposed modular alternatives. Buy American Act Compliance: Demonstration of domestic sourcing and manufacturing pathways compliant with BAA requirements. Schedule & Capacity: Current manufacturing lead times, production capacity, and feasibility of meeting the February 2027 delivery milestone. Budgetary Estimates: Preliminary Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) pricing. Vendor Information: Company legal name, primary point of contact (name, phone, email), SAM.gov Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CAGE Code, and business size/socioeconomic status under the applicable NAICS code(s). Submission Instructions: All responses must be received no later than Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time to Susan.Newcomb@faa.gov and Robert.Higgins@faa.gov. Please include the project title (Modular, Transportable Building Units or Shipping Containers � Key West, FL) in the subject line of your submission. 4. Disclaimer This market survey is issued for informational, market research, and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a Screening Information Request (SIR), Request for Proposals (RFP), or formal solicitation. The FAA is neither requesting nor accepting unsolicited proposals under this notice. The Government assumes no financial liability for any costs incurred by respondents in preparing, submitting, or following up on responses to this announcement. All submissions become the property of the FAA and will not be returned. Information obtained through this market survey may be utilized in future procurement activities supporting the Brand-New Air Traffic Control Initiative�a long-term infrastructure modernization effort to update the National Airspace System (NAS), including critical upgrades to Air Traffic Control Towers (ATCT) and Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON) facilities.

OBJECTIVES: The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, and incidentals necessary to perform smoke testing, hydro jetting and evaluations of the drain, waste and vent system. BACKGROUND: Buildings 34 and 42 has experienced an intermittent sewer odor throughout the facilities. The Government requires a comprehensive evaluation of the Drain, Waste, and Vent system to identify potential defects, leaks, obstructions, improper connections, and other deficiencies contributing to the odor. No repairs are authorized under this contract. The purpose of this effort is to document the existing condition of the entire DWV system and provide recommendations for future corrective actions. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS: Perform a complete smoke test of the entire DWV systems. o The Contractor shall introduce a non-toxic, non-staining plumbing smoke, or another industry approved standard testing medium, into the DWV systems. o The smoke used shall be specifically manufactured and intended for plumbing system testing. o If an alternative testing method is proposed, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the PM prior to use and demonstrate that the method provides an equivalent level of leak detection. o Identify and document all locations where smoke is observed. o The Contractor shall hydro jet the entire accessible sanitary drain systems, including horizontal mains, branch lines, building sewer and vertical stacks where practical. o The Contractor shall perform a CCTV inspection of the entire accessible DWV systems and provide a USB thumb drive with footage of the inspection. o Provide a comprehensive written inspection report and a summary of smoke test findings and a complete hydro jetting report. o No repairs shall be performed under this contract. o If conditions requiring repairs are identified, the Contractor shall document the deficiency and include the location and recommend corrective action in the final report. o Due to building occupancy, all work shall be performed after normal business hours. o Normal business hours are between 0600-1800, Monday-Friday. description: Description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Iqaluit, Nunavut Territories, has a requirement for Generator Inspection & Maintenance Services at the RCMP Cambridge Bay, Clyde River, Gjoa Haven, Kinngait, Qikitarjuaq, Taloyoak Detachments, Iqaluit Headquarters Building and Iqaluit Hangar. This procurement is subject to the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement and the Directive on Government Contracts, Including Real Property Leases, in the Nunavut Settlement Area. Bidders are requested to maximize Inuit employment, subcontracting and on-the-job training opportunities, and involve Inuit businesses, in carrying out the work under this project. The Nunavut Agreement contains a provision requiring the inclusion of socio-economic bid criteria in the solicitation document, when practicable and consistent with sound procurement management principles. These socio-economic bid criteria are referred to as Nunavut Benefits Criteria (NBC) and Inuit Benefits Criteria (IBC), and bidders propose Inuit benefits in their bid submission via an Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP). This solicitation is limited for bidding among firms registered on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). Bids submitted by businesses not on the IFR will render the bid non-responsive and no further consideration will be accorded to the bid. Delivery Date: The contract period will be for 36-months from the date of contract, with the option to extend for 2 additional 1 year periods. Security: This requirement contains a security requirement. Basis of selection: A bid must comply with all the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory requirements. Bids not meeting the requirements will be declared non-responsive. The selection will be based on the highest responsive combined rating of total Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP) merit, and price. The ratio will be 30% for the total IBP merit, and 70% for price. Tenders must be submitted to the RCMP Bid Receiving Unit at: NWR_Procurement_Bids@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Refer to the attached tender documents to obtain further information. Canada retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. It is the sole responsibility of the Bidder to regularly consult GETS for the most up-to-date information. Canada will not be liable for any oversight on the Bidder's part nor for notification services offered by a third party. title: Robins RAPID Construction OTA Progressive Design Build Fiber Replacement
description: FA8501-27-RAPID-CIRCUIT F1-170129-OTA Under the RAPID Umbrella Framework: RAPID Progressive Design-Build to Replace Circuit F-01 from Fowler Substation UHHZ170129 Description The Department of the Air Force, 78th Civil Engineer Group, Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, is issuing this Special Notice under the Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development (RAPID) umbrella framework and pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Government seeks industry Solution Briefs for an anticipated Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to Replace Circuit F-01 from Fowler Substation at Robins AFB, GA. The requirement includes replacement of all 15kV, 500MCM cable throughout circuit F-01. This will include replacement and removal all broken breakers or bad cable racks, install new bell ends on conduits, and pump water/dirt from manholes. This Special Notice is not an invitation for bids, a request for proposals under the Federal Acquisition Regulation, nor a commitment by the Government to make an award. Any resulting instrument will be an OTA for facility construction and repair under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Purpose The purpose of this Area of Interest is to obtain commercially viable, safe, and schedule-credible solutions to design plans for and to perform the replacement of expired high-risk Circuit F01 cabling in order to prevent operational risk, mission delays, and compounding economic costs due to infrastructure failure at Robins Air Force Base, Georgia. The Government requires an integrated approach to address the design, removal of deteriorated cables and replacement with new cable in The Fowler Substation. The selected approach must provide a practical path to execute the work while minimizing disruption to aircraft operations and controlling construction, safety, environmental, and schedule risks. Project Background and Existing Conditions Circuit F-01 has surpassed its operational lifecycle, creating a high-probability risk for catastrophic failure. If the remaining aged portion is not replaced, the installation faces risk of emergency repair premiums and disruption to sustaining airfield infrastructure, supporting safe aircraft movement, installation readiness, and continued mission operations. The work area is slightly congested and impacted by various airfield operations. The Fowler Substation Circuit F-01 will remain in full operation during the entire duration of the project by back feeding with circuit ties. Project Areas Phase 1 (Preconstruction & Collaborative Design): Collaborative design development stakeholders to achieve 65%, site surveys, risk mitigation planning, schedule and establishment of an open-book Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) IAW with all other aspects of the SOO. Phase 2 (Final Design & Construction Execution) Completion of final design and full construction execution (exercised upon agreement). Safely construct the facility/project within the agreed GMP and schedule. Assume hazardous materials exist. Address requirements for worker notification, abatement, and disposal. Employ a safety and health professional to provide a HASP per DoDI 6055.01. Comply with Robins Environmental Requirements (Section 01560) submitting Waste Management Report/Landfill Waste Tickets, Solid Waste Disposal Plan, and Qualified Recycling Program (QRP). Appropriately coordinate Stormwater & Erosion Control. Structure execution to allow for payable milestones payments, as well as all other aspects outlined in the SOO. Project-Specific Objectives and Phasing Replace all 15kV, 500MCM cable throughout the distribution of circuit F-01 in its entirety of multiple different installation facilities, while remaining in full operation besides outages and removing and replacing all broken breakers or bad cable racks, install new bell ends on conduits, and pump water/dirt from manholes. Address specific phasing to accommodate congested areas. OTA & RAPID Framework Approach This project is being executed as an Area of Interest (AOI) under the overarching RAPID (Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development) Umbrella Program Notice. In accordance with the RAPID framework, this project utilizes a Progressive Design-Build approach under the standalone statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Government will be expecting a 100% completed design package and/or specific phasing and repair requirements followed by the completion of the construction or performance of the designed actions. Competitive Selection Process Phase 1 Solution Brief Requirements The Government reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to determine that a response which does not conform to the requirements or instructions contained in this announcement is ineligible for further consideration. Interested respondents shall submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief in a clear, concise, and organized manner in accordance with this announcement. To facilitate an efficient review, responses shall be prepared in accordance with the instructions and formatting requirements contained in this announcement. Failure to comply with these requirements may increase the risk that the response will not be considered for further evaluation. The Government will evaluate them to identify the most highly qualified parties. Submission Requirement should be submitted by 3:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on or before 20 November 2026. Interested respondents shall submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief consisting of no more than five written pages (5), excluding the cover page. Email is the official form of submission for responses. Surety letters may be attached without counting towards 5 page limit. Page format should be 8.5 x 11. The Solution Brief shall include: Cover Page Company name UEI Mailing address Primary point of contact Email address and telephone number Identification of this RAPID AOI Executive Summary, Team Composition, and Organization Summary of the respondent�s qualifications and anticipated delivery capability Explanation of why the team is qualified for the anticipated requirement The team�s understanding of the Robins Air Force Base operational environment The team�s experience working in occupied facilities, congested site logistics, complex mechanical/electrical system integrations, and adherence to stringent environmental and safety standards. (e.g., hazardous material abatement, and experience with Department of War/Air Force Standards). The team�s proposed approach to Phase 1 collaboration and risk reduction Identification of any material capability, staffing, access, bonding, or teaming assumptions. Past Relevant Construction Capability and Experience Minimum Requirement: The Company must demonstrate a minimum of five (5) years of experience successfully executing construction projects of comparable size, scope, and complexity. Focus: Historical performance in occupied facilities, managing congested site logistics, complex mechanical/electrical system integrations, adhering to environmental and safety standards.(e.g., hazardous material abatement, and experience with Department of Defense/Air Force Standards). Note that while DoD experience is considered, it will not be a deciding factor in determining a firm more qualified. Financial Capacity and Bonding A statement of financial capacity to perform the anticipated work Current single-project and aggregate bonding capacity, if bonds are anticipated; Name of surety Any other information necessary to demonstrate capacity to perform the anticipated project. Construction Execution and Phasing Approach Methodology for physical work execution Utility outage coordination Evaluation & Selection Criteria The Government will utilize a two-step, Qualifications-Based Selection (QBS) process mapped to the RAPID framework to select the Design-Builder. In accordance with PDB methodology, price will not be evaluated during the initial selection process. Selection is based on qualifications, experience, and collaborative capabilities. Step 1: RAPID Phase 1 Equivalent Evaluation

title: USP Canaan IPS Supply and Startup
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP), USP Canaan, requires the furnishing and delivery of emergency lighting inverter systems and factory-authorized startup services. The Government shall perform installation under separate means. The Contractor shall not perform installation, demolition, wiring, removal of existing equipment, conduit work, or electrical construction. The products identified below are being procured on a Brand Name or Equal basis. Equal products must meet all salient characteristics contained in attached PWS for Myers Power Systems. To be considered for award, offers of 'equal' products must submit all descriptive literature and technical data necessary for the Contracting Officer to determine whether the product meets the salient characteristics specified in this solicitation. The submission must include the exact make, model, and manufacturer, alongside a cross-reference confirming compliance with each listed characteristic. Failure to provide sufficient technical evidence will result in the quote being determined technically unacceptable. Evaluation Factors Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose quotation represents the Best Value to the Government. The Government will evaluate quotations based on the following factors: Technical Compliance- The degree to which the proposed equipment meets or exceeds the salient characteristics and technical requirements identified in this solicitation, including the adequacy and completeness of supporting technical documentation and compliance with the Brand Name or Equal requirements. Delivery Schedule-The offeror's ability to meet or improve upon the Government's required delivery schedule, including proposed lead times for equipment delivery and startup services. Price-The total evaluated price for all CLINs. Past Performance- The Government may consider an offeror's past performance in supplying and delivering products similar in scope and complexity to the requirements of this solicitation. Evaluation may include the offeror's history of meeting delivery commitments, providing complete and accurate shipments, responding to customer concerns, and overall performance associated with the delivery of comparable equipment. Technical Compliance, Delivery Schedule, and Price, Past Performance will be considered in determining the quotation that represents the Best Value to the Government. The Government may award to other than the lowest-priced offeror if the additional value associated with a higher-rated quotation warrants the additional cost. Any contractor interested in obtaining a contract award with the Federal Bureau of Prisons must be registered at https://www.sam.gov/. Faith-Based and Community-Based Organizations have the right to submit offers equally with other organizations for contracts for which they are eligible. All responsible sources are encouraged to submit a written offer which will be considered for award. The solicitation will be available on or after November 6, 2026, with a due date of November 20, 2026 4:00 p.m. EST The solicitation will be distributed solely through the SAM beta.gov web site https://beta.sam.gov/ Hard copies of the solicitation document will not be available. The site provides downloading instructions. All future information about this acquisition, including solicitation amendments, will also be distributed solely through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure that they have the most up-to-date information about this acquisition. Offerors must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) and possess a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) at the time of quotation submission and throughout contract performance. To be eligible for award, an offeror must be identified in SAM as a small business concern under NAICS Code 335999. The Government will verify the offeror's SAM registration, UEI, size status, and exclusion records prior to award. Offerors shall include their UEI in their quotation and on any solicitation response forms submitted to the Government. Failure to maintain an active SAM registration, possess a valid UEI, or qualify as a small business concern under the applicable NAICS code may render the quotation ineligible for award. Pursuant to Wage Determination 2015-4257, the specialized technical services required for the emergency power system startup and commissioning have been mapped to the most applicable labor categories defined within the Department of Labor (DOL) SCA Directory of Occupations. Pursuant to the Service Contract Labor Standards (SCLS) statute, it has been determined that the official occupational classification for this procurement is Engineering Technician IV (Occupational Code 30084) Instructions to Offerors Offerors shall submit a completed Standard Form (SF) 1449, Solicitation/Contract/Order for Commercial Products and Commercial Services, with their quotation. All offerors shall submit their completed submission to both Chris Ficken, cficken@bop.gov and Joseph Kozuch, jkozuch@bop.gov. The offeror's Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) shall be entered in Block 17a of the SF 1449. The UEI provided on the SF 1449 must match the offeror's active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors shall include all technical documentation, product literature, warranty information, delivery lead times, and pricing necessary for the Government to evaluate the quotation. The Government will verify the apparent successful offeror's SAM registration, UEI, business size status, and eligibility for award prior to contract award. Failure to provide a completed SF 1449, including a valid UEI in Block 17a, may render a quotation ineligible for award.

Failure to provide sufficient technical evidence will result in the quote being determined technically unacceptable. Evaluation Factors Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose quotation represents the Best Value to the Government. Delivery Schedule-The offeror's ability to meet or improve upon the Government's required delivery schedule, including proposed lead times for equipment delivery and startup services. Price-The total evaluated price for all CLINs. Past Performance- The Government may consider an offeror's past performance in supplying and delivering products similar in scope and complexity to the requirements of this solicitation. Evaluation may include the offeror's history of meeting delivery commitments, providing complete and accurate shipments, responding to customer concerns, and overall performance associated with the delivery of comparable equipment. Technical Compliance, Delivery Schedule, and Price, Past Performance will be considered in determining the quotation that represents the Best Value to the Government. title: Commercial Solution Opportunity - Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) CONUS
description: In accordance with the Commercial Solutions Opening � Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA), posted October 2, 2026, under Notice ID HQCAAA2701, the following requirement supports Area of Interest (AoI) 5.1 Accelerate Eligible Patron Growth. The parent CSO with instructions is located at Related ID HQCAAA2701. The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is seeking innovative, commercial approaches for a digital storefront, in-store fulfillment, and delivery solution(s), hereinafter referred to as �DeCA2U�. The primary goal of DeCA2U is to deliver a seamless, modern, and fully integrated omnichannel grocery experience for authorized patrons at Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) locations in the contiguous United States (CONUS), Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico that matches or exceeds the best commercial grocery services available today. The DeCA2U solution shall utilize a market-aligned commercial financial model typical of leading grocery retailers. The prospective contractor shall identify all locations in which it could provide an entire end-to-end solution enabling authorized patrons to place grocery orders, make payment, and receive their groceries at a designated delivery location. Specifically, DeCA2U will provide one unified, easy-to-use platform enabling authorized patrons and military units to: Shop and order groceries online anytime, anywhere via mobile app or website; Receive accurate real-time inventory and pricing from their local commissary; Benefit from fast, accurate in-store picking and professional order assembly; Enjoy reliable, tracked doorstep delivery directly to their home or quarters or convenient curbside pickup; Track and be rewarded for purchases; Leverage value-added functionality like forgotten items, �People who bought this� recommendations, menu building, price checking, or any other shopping experience enhancement capability; and Complete transactions through a secure, seamless payment process supporting all tender types including, but not limited to, MILITARY STAR and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT). The Government reserves the right to add payment options. Offerors shall propose pricing reflecting current commercial market rates for similar omnichannel. The Service Contract Labor Standards (formerly the Service Contract Act), 41 U.S.C. ��6701 et seq. will be applicable to any resulting contract. The desired outcome is to establish a long-term commercial partnership that provides authorized commissary patrons with a convenient, reliable, and cost-effective grocery shopping experience through an integrated solution for online ordering, payment processing, order fulfillment, pickup, and delivery. The solution should leverage proven commercial capabilities, support operational efficiency, enhance the commissary benefit, and provide a scalable and sustainable service model that can adapt to evolving mission requirements and patron needs. Proposed solutions should comply with applicable commercial and/or Department of War (DoW) cybersecurity standards, including but not limited to, SOC 2 Type 2. Additionally, integrated payment and entitlement gateways supporting all tender types including, but not limited to, MILITARY STAR and SNAP EBT. Proposed solutions must meet current commercial PCI DSS compliance and USDA Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) digital security specifications. The platform shall ensure robust end-to-end encryption for data at rest and in transit (FIPS 140-3 validated) and secure patron Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in accordance with federal privacy standards. Solutions shall propose a Period of Performance (PoP) that reflects customary commercial lead times, development lifecycles, and delivery benchmarks for the proposed capability. The Government reserves the right to adjust the proposed PoP to align with mission requirements, funding availability, and applicable regulatory limitations, including structuring the award as a base period with one or more option periods at the Government�s discretion. DeCA will not endorse any contractor employee for the purpose of installation access; as such, solutions shall address their proposed approach to meeting applicable military installation access requirements, including personnel screening, credentialing, and delivery access procedures. DeCA will utilize the phased evaluation process established in the overarching Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), Notice ID HQCAAA2701. Interested vendors with demonstrated commercial experience in grocery eCommerce, order fulfillment, pickup, delivery, or integrated retail solutions with foundational information security management system standard should submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief in accordance with the applicable submission requirements of the overarching CSO. Solution Briefs should describe: the proposed commercial approach; relevant capabilities; anticipated benefits to DeCA and its authorized patrons; proposed business model; PoP; Service Contract Labor Standards; installation access; and cybersecurity measures. Additionally, all proposed solutions shall address the vendor's ability to integrate with DeCA�s retail ecosystems and scale to DeCA�s business needs. The Government will evaluate submissions in accordance with the criteria established in the overarching CSO and may invite selected vendors to participate in subsequent phases. The closing date for this �Call for Solution� is Friday 13 November 2026 at 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST). All communications, including solution brief information and submission requirements shall be sent via email to the following Points of Contact: Diana Gross-Bendall, email: diana.gross-bendall@deca.mil and Tinitia Gholson, email: tinitia.gholson@deca.mil.

title: NOTICE OF AWARD: Region VI Asbestos Abatement Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA)
description: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Region VI, has awarded Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) No. 70FBR626A00000002 to RNDI Companies, Inc., Rockwall, Texas, for asbestos abatement services supporting FEMA Region VI facilities in Denton, Texas. This BPA was awarded as a Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) sole-source acquisition in accordance with RFO FAR Part 19 and the applicable statutory small-business sole-source authority. In accordance with RFO 12.103, commercial acquisitions involving small-business programs are governed by RFO FAR Part 19. Further, RFO 6.103-5(e) provides that acquisitions authorized or required by statute under applicable small-business sole-source authorities do not require a public justification and approval under the standard Part 6 posting procedures. Accordingly, a publicly posted justification and approval was not required for this acquisition. The contract file includes an internal Contracting Officer determination documenting the market research conducted, review of available capability information, and the basis for determining that there was not a reasonable expectation of receiving offers from two or more eligible and capable WOSB concerns capable of meeting the complete requirement. The BPA establishes fixed pricing for asbestos-abatement services, including asbestos-containing material removal, containment, decontamination, high-efficiency particulate air vacuuming, negative-air controls, waste handling, transportation, disposal, regulatory notifications, final cleaning, clearance support, and related services. The BPA base period is September 24, 2026, through September 23, 2027, with four one-year option periods. The total BPA ceiling, including the base period and all option periods, is $300,000.00. This BPA does not obligate funds and does not guarantee a minimum quantity or dollar value of work. Funds will be obligated only through individual call orders issued under the BPA. title: IT Professional Services
description: The Canada Council for the Arts' Information Technology section requires access to qualified professional services providers to support ongoing IT operational requirements and project-based initiatives on an as-and-when-required basis. General requirement The Contractor must provide information technology professional services, on an as-and-when-requested basis, in support of the Canada Council’s operational, maintenance, enhancement, modernization, transformation and advisory requirements. The Contractor must actively support knowledge transfer to Canada Council personnel proportionate to the scope, complexity and duration of each engagement. Deliverables, documentation, training materials, presentations, knowledge transfer activities and related services may be required in English, French or both official languages, as specified in the applicable call-up. The Contractor must provide qualified resources, perform the authorized work and deliver all required outputs in accordance with the requirements of the Standing Offer and the applicable call-up. The Contractor must provide professional services in information technology across one or more of the following service streams: Stream 1 - Enterprise platforms and business applications Services may include the configuration, development, administration, enhancement, integration, maintenance and support of enterprise platforms and business applications, including Microsoft, Salesforce and Unit4 technologies. Stream 2 - Applications, integration and support Services may include the design, development, modernization, testing, deployment, integration, maintenance and support of custom-developed and commercial off-the-shelf applications, interfaces and related components. Stream 3 - Data, analytics and information management Services may include data architecture, data analysis, reporting, analytics, business intelligence, information management, database administration, data governance and data integration. Stream 4 - Architecture, cloud, infrastructure and cybersecurity Services may include enterprise, solution and integration architecture; cloud architecture and infrastructure; cybersecurity; identity and access management; network services; and related advisory, implementation and support activities. Stream 5 - Project, Program and Change Management Support Services may include project and program management, project coordination, business and functional analysis, business process analysis, organizational change management, planning, governance, performance reporting and stakeholder engagement, documentation, knowledge transfer and training services. Stream 6 - User experience, accessibility and quality assurance Services may include user experience design, AI-enabled user experience and service design, accessibility assessment and remediation, testing and quality assurance. Stream 7 - Audit and advisory services Services may include audit and advisory services related to technology controls, compliance, governance, risk management, cybersecurity, platforms, applications, processes and IT operations. Stream 8 - Artificial intelligence, automation and emerging technologies Services may include, in accordance with the Government of Canada's artificial intelligence strategy, artificial intelligence strategy development, generative AI and machine learning advisory services, AI solution design and implementation, responsible AI governance, automation, intelligent search, knowledge management, AI-assisted service delivery, model evaluation, data readiness, and emerging technology assessment.

title: Germany – Systems and technical consultancy services – 10017688 - National Information Sharing and Analysis Framework
description: InnoPA: Supporting e-Government and Innovation in the Public Administration Supporting eGovernment and Innovation in Public Administration (InnoPA) is a joint project implemented by the German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ) in Egypt, on behalf of the German Federal Government, and in partnership with the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT). The project aims to strengthen the capacities of the public sector and civil society to drive an inclusive and responsive digital transformation in line with European standards. The InnoPA project implements a variety of interventions in the areas of institutional capacity building, innovation promotion, digital inclusion, and policy support. The project adopts the principle of "leave no one behind" to ensure that all segments of society benefit from the digital transformation process and enjoy an effective and responsive public administration. The project has three pillars: 1) Support an inclusive, citizen-centered digital transformation of the public sector, the project aims to bridge the digital divide and increase the uptake of existing digital public services. To this end, collaborations with civil society organizations will be carried out to enhance the digital skills of both citizens and civil servants, alongside additional measures focused on strengthening institutional capacity. 2) promotes innovative solutions for the inclusive and citizen-oriented digital transformation of the public sector. A key part of this effort is the GovTech Innovation Programme, which accelerates startups and the creation of inclusive technological products that enhance government services and responsiveness to citizens' needs and 3) provides support for the development of forward-looking digital strategies and legal frameworks in emerging areas such as trust services, artificial intelligence, and data-driven decision-making, in line with EU digitalization standards. EU-German Action Digital Transformation in the Southern Neighbourhood The programme "Digital Transformation in the Southern Neighbourhood" was initiated in February 2026 and is co-funded by the European Commission Directorate General MENA (DG MENA), the German Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), and the German Federal Foreign Office (FFO). The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) has been commissioned to implement the three project components and implements the activities from Germany, Spain and additional regional hubs. In partnership with governments in the region, the programme strives to accelerate the Southern Neighbourhood"s digital transformation through targeted support across three critical areas: cybersecurity, digital regulation, and digital skills. The second specific objective on improved Prevention, preparedness and response of relevant stakeholders in the South-ern Neighbourhood with regards to cyber threats is pertinent for this tender. It comprises the following pillars: 1. Strengthened national legal frameworks and cybersecurity governance in line with international standards and frameworks for responsible state behaviour in cyberspace. Support will include technical assistance for the drafting, revision and implementation of national cybersecurity strategies, laws, and policies, in line with international frameworks and the EU"s Cybersecurity Strategy. 2. Improved operational capacities, such as prevention, preparedness and response, for cyber incident management and inter-agency cooperation. This includes hands-on training, development of operational procedures, provision of technical tools, and facilitation of simulation exercises to improve threat response and incident management. 3. Established community of stakeholders for sharing best practices and incident information at regional, trans-regional and international level. In this framework joint activities such as regional table-top exercises, joint threat analysis workshops, and mentorship programmes for mid-career professionals will be explored.

Additionally, the team has developed specialized software programs, operational processes, and analytical algorithms necessary to support instrument performance assessment, data processing, and scientific interpretation. description: HANKINNAN KOHDE Hankinnan kohteena verkkosivuston toteutus ja ylläpito tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä määritellyn mukaisesti. Hankinnan kohteena on WordPress-julkaisujärjestelmällä tai vastaavalla avoimen lähdekoodin julkaisujärjestelmällä toteutettava uusi prh.fi-verkkosivusto. Hankintaan kuuluu sivuston tekninen toteutus valmiiden suunnitelmien pohjalta sekä jatkuvat tuki-, ylläpito- ja kehittämispalvelut. Hankinnan tavoitteena on toteuttaa moderni, luotettava ja helposti ylläpidettävä verkkosivusto, joka ohjaa asiakkaiden toimintaa ja asiointia sekä toimii Patentti- ja rekisterihallituksen pääviestintäkanavana. Tavoitteena on laadukas käyttäjäkokemus, palvelun jatkuva toimivuus sekä verkkosivuston kehittäminen myös tulevaisuudessa. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä, erityisesti liitteessä 1 "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus". SOPIMUSKAUSI Tavoitteena on, että sopimus tulee voimaan tammikuussa 2027. Sopimus on ensin voimassa määräaikaisena kaksi (2) vuotta, minkä jälkeen sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi. Ks. myös tarjouspyynnön liitteenä A olevan sopimuksen kohta 5. HANKINNAN LAAJUUS Hankinnan laajuus käy ilmi tarjouspyynnöstä ja sen liitteistä. Hansel Oy toimii tässä hankinnassa konsultoivassa roolissa.

The Correctional Service Canada – CORCAN Ontario Region has a requirement for monthly rental of highway trailers. Deliver the replacement trailer within two (2) business days from receipt of notification from the Project Authority; 6. Include *unlimited kilometres during the rental periods for each trailer. Note: *CSC requires trailers with unlimited kilometres as part of the trailer rental. description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT (NPP) For TASK BASED INFORMATICS PROFESSIONAL SERVICES (TBIPS) UNSPSC: 80101500 TBIPS Grants and Contributions Transformation Initiative (GCTI) – Stream 1 B.1 Business Analysis Services and Stream 2 A.11 Tester, P.11 Quality Assurance Reference Number: 27-320449 Solicitation Number: 27-320449 Organization Name: Department of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development Solicitation Date: 2026-11-03 Closing Date: 2026–11-25 @2:00 PM Anticipated Start Date: 2027-01-15 Estimated Delivery Date: 2030–01-15 Estimate Level of Effort: 5,280 days for an estimated eight (8) resources Contract Duration: The contract period will be for an estimated thirty six months from the date of contract Solicitation Method: Competitive Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement Applies: No Number of Contracts: One Applicable Trade Agreements: • The Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) • The Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA), • Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) • The Canada-Columbia Free Trade Agreement (CColFTA), • Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) • Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement (CHFTA) • Canada Korea Free Trade Agreement (CKFTA) • The Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA), • The Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement (CPanFTA) • Canada Ukraine Free Trade Agreement (CUFTA) • World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP), Requirement Details Tendering Procedure: Selective Tendering This requirement is open only to those TBIPS Supply Arrangement Holders who qualified under Tier 1 for services in the National Capital Region for the following categories Stream 1 – B.1 Business Analyst Level 3 Stream 2 – A.11 Tester Level 2 P.11 Quality Assurance Specialist Level 2 and Level 3. (Conditional PSIB) The following SA Holders have been invited to submit a proposal: Cogniva Information Solutions Inc. EMINENT SYSTEMS INC. Factr Limited, ALTIS RECRUITMENT & TECHNOLOGY INC., in Joint Venture Green PI Inc Jumping Elephants Incorporated Maplestream Inc., Cofomo Inc. IN JOINT VENTURE Maverin Business Services Inc. Newfound Recruiting Corporation Outwitly Inc QMR Staffing Solutions Incorporated SYSTEMATIX SOLUTIONS TI INC/SYSTEMATIX IT SOLUTIONS INC Systemscope Inc. Tato Recruiting Inc., S.I. SYSTEMS ULC, in Joint Venture TECSIS Corporation Wiz Management Inc Description of Work: DFATD is building a modern and user-friendly Grants & Contributions platform that will effectively deliver and manage consistent data across an enterprise which will facilitate greater innovation To support the successful delivery of the GCTI initiative, DFATD requires specialized User Experience (UX/UI Designer), Testing, and Quality Assurance resources. These resources will work within multidisciplinary Agile teams to support the design, development, validation, testing, and continuous improvement of the enterprise Grants and Contributions platform. UX resources will conduct user research, analyze user needs, develop user journeys, create wireframes and prototypes, perform usability evaluations, assess accessibility requirements, and provide recommendations that support intuitive and user-centered digital services. Testing and Quality Assurance resources will develop and execute test plans and test cases, perform functional, integration, regression, usability, and accessibility testing, manage defects, support solution validation activities, and help ensure the quality and reliability of delivered solutions. Together, these resources will help ensure that the platform delivers a high-quality, accessible, reliable, and user-focused experience while meeting business, technical, and operational requirements. This requirement to provide an estimated two (2) Business Analysts level 3 for Stream 1 and two (2) Testers and four (4) Quality Assurance resources for Stream 2. No contract will be awarded until the applicable security requirements have been established and satisfied. Bidders should note that personnel and/or organizational security screening requirements will apply and must be met prior to contract award and/or commencement of work.
